scores.why: This is the Signal Box line language the owner asked for, carried through every page with restraint. Home has a Coming up track with a lit now lamp, setup steps on a track and a To do timetable with amber lamps; Chat hangs from Vera's mark to a green ring at the box; each page icon has its ring-and-bracket head; the bar has a dot under the current page; Status has a chain for who answers. It sits on grounded slate with a measured steel-cyan (a period colour, green share 54%, neon 3.7%) and keeps the greeting's pool and the glowing now lamp. The tube light is only moderately restored.

It is Signal Legend, which the owner singled out, with the phosphor switched back on: a layered halo on 'mind', blooming monitors, glowing lamps set in dark slots, a lit latest bubble and a now lamp on each page. It keeps the Coming up track, the chat rail and the legends set into the rails. The page still reads mostly green and grey (77% green share), and the To do track with lamps, the bar dot and the page-icon bracket are missing.

Flight Deck, which the owner loved, with the tubes relit. The lit-versus-matte discipline gives exactly 'light where attention belongs', and cyan for the family's hand is period-true. It lacks the order-carrying tracks the owner prizes, and mono caps legends on every row ('ACTIVITY FOR MAYA, THEO') make it busy.

A beautiful, modern and well-labelled page that the owner named, with the Coming up track and legends set into the rails. It is greyer and less lit than its Relit child, so it loses to it on the owner's latest word.
The owner's favourite colour code and fine demarcation lines, but its tubes are calmer than the owner now wants. Caps legends on actions and rows still weigh on it.

A well-finished listing: heads on one line, true columns, a now lamp, and a quiet pewter L to each band that hints at line art. Its colour is Programme Guide's, it brings back no light beyond it, and its CRT soul lives mostly in the monitors.
A calm, well-typeset TV listing with the tuning scale under the bar. It has none of the Signal Box tracks and only modest glow, so it reads as a handsome modern listing rather than a lit tube.

The service-manual leaders and numbered steps are fine line art in the owner's taste. The '80 COL / 25 LN' dimensions are costume, and at a glance the page is still Programme Guide with no extra light.

A bold, legible idea the owner would like the bones of: Vera's line down Home and a Chat timetable with stops. It also has a raster-lit departure board. It spends too many colours: five enamel discs in the bar, yellow arrow tiles, a hazard stripe, copper-brown family bubbles and a yellow cap on Status. That makes the companions compete with the green instead of supporting it, and the greeting has lost its green pool.
A tidier type scale and slashed zeros are a real typesetting gain the owner would enjoy up close. Otherwise it is identical to Reverse Video, with no lines and no restored light.
A coherent text-mode grammar with a steel reverse block. It has none of the order-carrying tracks, its glow is modest, and it now sits behind the Signal and Flight families.

Docking the machine in one lit glass column with a green pool is a strong CRT move and a genuinely new structure. Indigo keys everywhere, including five heavy 'ALL →' keys on Home, are 'more blue than necessary' and a violet-blue that feels off-period beside the green.

The oscilloscope drawing the family's four weeks is the most period-true CRT picture on the panel, and its engraved frames with legends in the line are kin to the owner's line art. Several things work against it: the whole page is lifted to a grey-green panel, the brushed-aluminium nameplates glare, the oxblood knobs and rose avatars are the pink the owner dislikes, and wide-tracked caps run everywhere.

The operator-manual figures are clever fine-line drawings of the page's own data. The underlined blue links on every title, the paper-grey reverse cells and the heavy double-rule focus make it read cold and technical, and there is little tube light outside the radar.

The cyan night light is a period colour with a clear job. Newsreader serif titles and the bookish graphite plates move the page away from a green-screen terminal, and its CRT lives only in the monitors.

The constellation figures are charming. Fraunces serif, cobalt-navy plates and a centred book column make it a storybook night sky rather than a phosphor terminal, and there is more blue than the owner wants.

The waveform on the Next up tube is lovely CRT. The warm graphite faceplates read as the brown the owner called off-motif, the red needle and lowercase labels pull away from the green-screen character, and many targets are small.
Keys and wells are nicely tactile. The teal-tinted bands make the page one blue-green family with the phosphor instead of a grounded support for it.
Serif body text on a starfield in one centred column is the least CRT page here. Its green is confined to the console.
Today's page still has the tube's glow, but the owner's first ask stands: all bright green on black, too contrasty, near-monochrome (83% green), with no grounded colour or structural line art.

fixes.suggestion: Keep every track exactly as drawn: the Coming up track with its now lamp, the setup track, the To do timetable lamps, Lately added's drop line, the chat thread ending in a green ring, the ring-and-bracket page head and the bar dot. What it needs is the owner's latest ask, the light brought back where the phosphor is. Raise the monitors to screenGlow 0.95-1.0 with the kit's scanlines, sheen and three-halo VT323. Give 'mind' the full E1 two-layer halo. Make every green lamp (now, Status, today on the month) a glowing dot with a tight and a wide halo (0 0 4px brand/0.8, 0 0 12px brand/0.35), breathing only where it means live. Neutralise the warm kind tints on the Lately added and Ideas plates (Restaurant and Seasonal read brownish) to plain slate, and keep the kind colour in the ring lamp alone. Once the view passes 'late', turn the To do page's late lamps amber as Home's are.

Keep the relit tubes, lamps and halo. Graft in Track Diagram's line art where there is order: a vertical To do track with lamps in the timetable margin, the chat thread ending in a lit green ring at the message box, a ring-and-bracket round each page's icon, and a dot under the current page in the bar. Nudge the steel slightly toward cyan (about #9cc4dc) and give the slate a touch more of it on surfaces, so the page is less green-and-grey at a glance (green share 77% now).

Keep the lit instruments on matte plates and the cyan family hand. Add order-carrying tracks in the weight of the demarcation lines: Coming up as a track from a lit now lamp, and the chat thread hanging from Vera's glyph. Replace the mono caps meta above each row ('ACTIVITY FOR MAYA, THEO') with sentence-case meta under the title, and keep caps for the plate legends only.

Keep Vera's line down Home's middle and the Chat timetable, since they are the owner's favourite element, and keep the raster-lit departure board. Cut the colour count. Make the bar numbers plain ink discs, with only the current line in its enamel. Swap the yellow arrow tiles for plain steel arrows. Replace the hazard stripe with one thin amber rule. Put the family's bubbles on slate with only a copper initial, because the copper-brown tint is off-motif. Drop the yellow cap on Status, and restore the green pool under the greeting.

Keep the scope that draws the family's weeks, the engraved frames with the legend in the top line, and the trigger. Put the ground back on green-black (#0b0e0d) with the plates as slate, not a lifted grey-green panel. Make the nameplates dark engraved plates, not bright brushed aluminium. Replace the oxblood knobs and rose avatars with slate and steel. Keep wide-tracked caps to the frame legends only.

Keep the docked glass column with its green pool, since that is where the machine lives. Make the family's desk grounded slate keys with a single steel-cyan latched 'here', and drop indigo as a fill. Set 'All plans' and the other see-more links as underlined text links, not five 44px indigo keys.

judges.notes:
Through the owner's lens, the owner's latest word ('bring back some of the original phosphor effect') and the standing wish for Signal Box's line art both point at the same pair.

- **Track Diagram** is the first entrant since round 7 to carry that line language through every page with restraint. It has lines only where there is order, a lit now lamp at the start, a ring-and-bracket page head, the bar dot, and Chat hung from Vera's mark. It does this on grounded slate with a measured, period steel-cyan.
- **Signal Legend Relit** and **Flight Deck, Lit** answer the glow ask best. They show the kit's bloom, halos and glowing lamps kept to where the phosphor is, and it reads as light where attention belongs, not glare.

The ideal next round breeds the two: Track Diagram's tracks with Relit's tube light.

Among the wild entrants, the most promising reaches are:
- **Night Timetable:** Vera's line as the spine of Home.
- **Bench Scope:** the scope drawing the family's own data.
- **Docked Terminal:** the machine docked in one lit glass column.

All three lose on colour. That means too many companions, brown or copper surfaces, pink and oxblood, or too much indigo, rather than on structure.

Serif titles (Atlas After Hours, Figured Atlas) and warm hi-fi graphite (Braun Signal) drift furthest from the green-screen soul.

Today's page is scored at 4.0 as the yardstick, so the best has come about 5 points.

scores.why: The yardstick, held at round 9's 4.0. All the light the owner misses is here: the layered halo on 'mind' and Send, the greeting lit from below through scanlines, the blooming tubes, the lamps. But the whole page glows, so it is still the Matrix: glare, monochrome, and nothing grounded below the fold.

Answers the owner's latest word best. The original light is back only where the phosphor is: a two-layer halo on 'mind', Send and the typed-in box, the greeting's pool, tubes at full bloom with their spill, a breathing NOW lamp on the fortnight line, and Status lamps glowing in dark slots. Slate trays, steel keys and amber stay matte, so it is lit and alive without glare. It loses a little because To do has no light of its own and Home runs 1853px.

The lit-versus-matte discipline is the soul thesis made into a system. The screwed-faceplate tubes bloom, blur and scan like real phosphor, with a chin, vents and a power LED, while the family's plates stay matte and cyan never glows. It loses points for mono-caps legends in the demarcation lines that shout, a boxed TODAY that breaks the tube's bracket idiom, and a Next up that wraps 'Tuesday 29 / September' badly.

The best-finished listing: glass greeting with its cobalt corner, a thin grooved case with vents, the tuning scale, and a breathing now lamp beside the next plan. But its tubes run at screen #74f0a3 and 0.8 glow, so their halos are visibly thinner than today's. That dimming is exactly what the owner says was lost.

A signal box's lamps suit the kit's glowing-dots motif: the green now lamp at the head of the fortnight, amber lamps for overdue tasks, and lamps on Status's chain of who answers. The glass greeting is kept. The stop rings are unlit steel, so the diagram reads drawn rather than lit, and the tubes keep the dimmed 0.8 bloom.

Still a calm TV listing lit by one green tube, with the best case and the tuning scale. Measured against the owner's new ask it is now short of light: dimmed tubes, no halo on the typed-in box, and one small lamp below the fold. Evening Listing and the relit mutants supersede it.

Faithful keeper of the breathing now lamp and the text-mode grammar, but its child Relit does everything it does and switches the tubes back on. At 0.8 screen glow its page now reads grey-steel more than lit.
The most period grammar (frame legends, reverse video) and a green-edged ask box at rest. But the tubes are dimmed, steel windows fill Status, and the light is the least of the carried leaders'.

Reverse Video with a tidier type scale and slashed zeros on the machine's figures, which is period-true. The soul is unchanged from its parent: the tubes are still dimmed. The schoolbook a and g make the family's words a touch softer and less machine.

The service-manual pen is honest period kin, and dimensioning a monitor '80 COL / 25 LN' is a nice nod. But it is costume drawn beside the tube, not light in it: no glow is restored, and the tubes stay dimmed.

An oscilloscope is a green phosphor CRT, and here the trace draws the family's own coming weeks as glowing pulses. That is light that means something, the most alive new idea on the panel. It is held back because the lit glass greeting is gone, the scope's words are crisp mono with little bloom rather than VT323 halos, the olive-grey panel greys the black, and the brushed nameplates and extended caps are loud.

Giving the machine one lit glass column, with the pool rising from its foot, is the owner's 'light where attention belongs' made into layout, and a strong idea. But raised indigo keys fill the family's side, so starters and 'ALL PLANS' read as Bootstrap navy. The tube is small and dimmed at 0.8, and short pages leave dead black under the column.

The glass greeting returns with the green airglow at its horizon, and the tube gets the roll-bar power-on at full strength. But Newsreader titles, star discs and a cyan night light pull the page toward a book. Status is three plain plates with little light.

The dot-matrix departure board glows brightly, and Vera's line with lit rings is a real idea. But the glass greeting pool is gone. Pastel numbered roundels, a rainbow rule under the bar, yellow arrow tiles and a hazard stripe turn it into a transit wayfinding app, and the calm-green rail runs the whole column (bright-green pixels 7.3 per mille, the highest). The CRT becomes a guest.
Unchanged: the power-on roll bar and the keys are good CRT kin, but the teal-graphite ground makes one blue-green family with the phosphor and dulls the jump.

An operator's manual is honest terminal-era kin, and 'mind' still glows. But the figures are unlit blueprint drawings and the glass greeting is gone. The only tube is a portrait panel with no real case, so the page reads flat and ruled rather than lit.

The seismograph Next up is a lovely live trace. But the tube's words are a thin, dim dot-matrix, a red 'today' pill and needle sit inside the green glass, the greeting is a flat plate, and the warm brown graphite greys the black. It reads as a hi-fi faceplate, not a green screen.

The constellation charts are charming and the italic glowing 'mind' is lovely. But a navy starfield book in serif, with a wide strip of tube in a cobalt plastic case, leaves the phosphor a guest in someone else's page.
As in round 9: handsome and calm, with a lovely airglow, but a book about the night sky with no glass greeting and a cobalt case.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the relight kit whole: exact #6dff9c screens at 1.0, halos only on the phosphor list, lamps named on every page. Give To do its one light: a breathing now line in the timetable margin between the overdue and upcoming rows. Swap Coming up's tall cards for Programme Guide's one-line rows to bring Home near 1650px. Give the steel a breath more chroma (about #9fb9cc) so the page reads less grey. Pull the lemon and amber kind words down in chroma to cut the 38% neon in the non-green colour.

Keep the lit-versus-matte rule and the screwed faceplate with chin and LEDs. Set the demarcation legends in sentence-case Plex Sans 600, not mono caps. Keep the tube's own [TODAY] bright bracket instead of a boxed inverse. Stop Next up breaking 'Tuesday 29 / September', either by setting the date line nowrap or by narrowing the scope.

Change only the light: tubes to exact #6dff9c with screenGlow 1.0 (three halos and the 0.35px blur), the typed-in box's ring and bloom back, and scanlines in the greeting pool. The listing is finished; its tubes are what the owner misses.

Raise the tubes to 1.0. Let a stop lamp light for 0.12s and fade over 1.2s when its row is hovered, which is the afterglow the kit describes, and keep the rings steel at rest. Light the ring where it is your turn at the message box as a true glowing dot.

Keep the scope that draws the family's weeks, the rose trigger and the PHOSPHOR plate. Set the scope's words in VT323 with the three-halo bloom, and give Vera's frame a lit glass pool rising from its foot. Cool the panel from olive grey to slate (h about 230) so the black stays black. Replace the brushed nameplates and extended caps with legends knocked into the frame in Plex Mono 500 at .72rem. Keep the oxblood knobs to Home only.

Keep the machine's glass column and make it full-height and sticky, so its pool meets the foot and no black is left under it. Let the tube fill the column at 4:3 and full glow. Replace filled indigo key faces with slate keys that have a 2px indigo cap, keeping indigo as the hand without painting the desk navy.

Keep the three-column Home and Vera's line. Put the glass greeting pool back behind the ask stop. Drop the hazard stripe and the rainbow rule under the bar. Set the line numbers as steel numerals rather than pastel roundels. Use VT323 on the departure board so it reads as a green screen, not an LED sign.

judges.notes:
Through the soul lens this round turns on the owner's latest word, and the relit mutants answer it. Signal Legend Relit and Flight Deck, Lit show the original light can come back without the glare. Exact #6dff9c tubes at 1.0 glow and the layered halo on the few phosphor things ('mind', Send, the typed-in box, the monitors and the lamps) return the lit and alive feel, because everything else stays matte slate, steel or cyan. Scarcity comes from the list of lit things, not from dimming them. The carried leaders' 0.8 screen glow and #74f0a3 screens are now the biggest single soul deficit on the panel: put side by side at 1.6x, their tubes' halos are visibly thinner than today's.

The wild entrants all changed the whole page, which the owner rewards. But three of four dropped the lit glass greeting, which this lens has called load-bearing since round 8. Bench Scope has the best new idea for the soul: the tube draws the family's own data as a glowing trace. Docked Terminal's machine column is the best new layout for the soul. Both need the fixes above more than a new direction.

Recommendation for the standard: Programme Guide or Signal Legend structure plus Relit's light kit, with glow numbers at 1.0 on the phosphor list only, and one named lamp per page where something is live. Today's yardstick is held at 4.0 for comparability.

Crops I made are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/myjudge10/ (mon_*.png compares the tubes at 1.6x, lamps.png the lamps, ask.png the halo on 'mind' and Send).

scores.why: The yardstick. It has a real signature (a lit tube, a layered halo, the radar), but it is one green idea spread over a generic rounded-card dark mode. It is monochrome, and that is why the family said 'Matrix'.

The clearest new mood of the round: quiet Rams-era hi-fi. Warm graphite faceplates, lowercase printed labels, a green VFD Next up tracing the coming weeks as a signal, and the rule 'every measure is a dial' (drive-time dial on Ideas, month dial on Plans, a needle gauge for spend, a meter for To do). Add the toggle, the red 'now' needle and the radio-with-grille sign-in and it is grounded, tasteful and memorable. Its weak spots are Home's structure, which is still today's card grid, and page titles that are a little small.

A station at night, and a genuine system: numbered enamel lines (1 Vera ... 5 Wishes) with one colour each, Vera's conversation drawn as the main line with the ways to start as stops and 'Continue with Vera' as the terminus, dot-matrix departure boards for the phosphor, copper for people. It has confident big grotesque heads and the most joy of any entry. It loses a little on the loud yellow arrow tiles, the hazard stripe and the heavy boxed title plates.

The most rigorous invention: an operator's manual with numbered chapters and plates, each led by a figure drawn from the family's own data on grid paper (the family tree to Vera to 5/12/4, the late-bars chart, the setup rungs, the Status wiring diagram). It has paper-grey reverse video and a CRT roll-on power-up. The typography is excellent. But blue underlines on every row title make it read like raw HTML, and the mood is clever and cool rather than warm.

An oscilloscope is the truest green-phosphor instrument, and the scope that draws plans as pulses (with Ideas in XY mode) is inspired. Engraved frame legends, aluminium nameplates, oxblood knobs and the trace-smile sign-in give it a strong character. But the one-size type rule flattens the greeting to 15px, and tracked caps on disclosures, buttons and heads tip it towards costume.

The most storybook entry. The constellation figures for each kind, the kind filter drawn as a star chart and Fraunces with an italic glowing 'mind' are all lovely. The single centred column leaves half the desktop empty and makes Home 2800px long, the starfield is decoration, and Status and Chat are barely touched.

A handsome evening-magazine page: Newsreader titles over a grotesque, graphite plates, a cyan night light for the way on, a coloured disc per part and an airglow under the lit greeting. It hangs together and is warm, but the atlas idea reads faintly beyond the serif and the dots.

The best-finished listing: steel reverse video for here, tabular fact columns, links that look like links, a pewter L to each band. As style it is refined and calm, but it is the slate-and-steel mood the panel has seen for three rounds, and it is refinement rather than a new identity.

The boldest structural answer to the owner's direction: the machine gets one lit glass column (her question, Next up, the radar, the spend tube) docked beside a grounded slate desk. Chat split into her column and the thread is fresh. The indigo keys are heavy and a little stock-navy (five 44px 'ALL →' keys on Home), and short columns leave dead black under the glass.

A signal-box diagram with lines only where there is order. The fortnight runs across Home from a lit now lamp, To do hangs on a timetable, and Chat hangs from her screen to a ring at the box, which is lovely. The steel-cyan-on-slate palette is the familiar one, and the page still reads a bit like a transit map drawn over cards.
The TV listing set in type is still a considered identity, but its own finished child and the new wild entries now out-style it.

Flight Deck with the tubes blooming again. Matte versus lit is the right discipline, but at page scale it is the parent with glowing monitors. The caps mono legends keep it technical rather than charming.

Signal Legend with a relit halo, the fortnight now-lamp line and backlit steel keys. It is a tidy system and gets the light back where it belongs, but the mood is the same grey-steel slate as its siblings.
A calm, well-labelled signal box, but its low-chroma steel makes the page read grey. The relit child improves on it.
The EFIS colour code is well argued. Stylistically it is a competent cockpit with too many small caps legends.

The service-manual pen (callouts, '80 COL / 25 LN', numbered balloons) is a charming idea, but it is so faint that at page scale this is Programme Guide. The dimensions are costume that tells the family nothing.
The text-mode window grammar is clever, but the look is now dated against this round, and the difference from today is mostly frames.
A type-only reset (a major-third scale, schoolbook a and g, slashed zeros). It is a laudable typesetting exercise, but it is invisible at page scale and makes secondary text smaller.
The bookish serif atlas has a mood, but it is a thin, empty centred column with starfields. Its figured child now carries the idea much better.
The teal-graphite arcade bands read as one blue-green family with the phosphor, a fairly stock dark dashboard. The roll bar and the keys were its only lasting ideas.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the warm graphite faceplates, the green VFD tube with its signal trace and red now needle, the rule 'every measure is a dial' (weeks, drive time, month, spend gauge, to-do meter), the little signal glyph after each head, the toggle and the radio sign-in. Fix, in four parts. (1) Home's structure is still today's two-column card grid: let one long fortnight dial head Coming up, and set the lists as printed rows on the faceplate rather than cards inside cards. (2) Give page titles one more step (about 2.4rem, tighter tracking) so lowercase keeps its hierarchy, and keep lowercase to labels and heads. (3) Pull the plate chroma down a touch (C about 0.006) so it reads as anodised graphite, not brown. (4) Restore the tube's own light: scanlines, a faint bloom under Send, and the pool at the case's foot. Then lift targets from 40 to 44px.

Keep: the numbered enamel lines and their one colour each, Vera's line with its stops and terminus, the dot-matrix departure boards, copper for people, the segmented colour rule under the bar, and the bold grotesque. Fix: (1) turn the filled yellow arrow tiles into plain yellow arrows or underlines, since yellow shows the way and should not shout; (2) replace the hazard stripe with one amber rule, because amber already means 'needs a look'; (3) drop the boxed title plates and keep the roundel and the coloured top rule; (4) give Next up back its radar on Home, and bring Lately added under the terminus so the middle column does not end 700px early; (5) set the heads one weight lighter.

Keep: the chapters and plates, the figures drawn from data in the margin, paper-grey reverse video for 'here', and the roll-on power-up. Fix: take the underline off row titles (ink titles, a blue arrow or hover underline) so lists stop reading as raw HTML. Add one warm companion to the blueprint so the manual feels like a family's (the amber is already there; a warm paper for 'here' would do). Fill the empty space right of tall heads by letting the figure sit beside the title, and make phone figures readable (a summary strip rather than a thumbnail).

Keep: the scope drawing the family's own data, the engraved frame legends, the aluminium nameplate, the oxblood knobs as the family's hand, and the trace sign-in. Fix: allow a second size for the one voice that needs it (the question at about 1.6rem) and set disclosures and buttons in sentence case, keeping extended caps only for the legends in frame lines. Use fewer screws and bezel knobs. Draw the scope's pulses at varying heights, for example by duration, so the picture says more than 'one a day'.

The docked glass column is the best layout idea for 'green where it's needed, grounded elsewhere'. Keep it. Make it full height and sticky, with its green pool at the foot, so no switched-off black sits under it. Replace the five indigo 'ALL →' keys with text links, keeping keys for real actions. Lower the indigo's saturation so it reads as ink rather than stock navy UI.

Keep the constellation figures, the star-chart kind filter and the italic lit 'mind'. Break the single column on desktop: figures and lists in two columns, with the tube beside the question. Carry the figures onto Coming up (from the idea's kind) and give Status a figure of its own. Drop the starfield background.

judges.notes:
Through this lens, the four wild entrants are the first in several rounds to give the page a new mood rather than a new trim, and all four change Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas and Status, which is what the owner asked for. They also bring the phosphor back as it should come: as the machine's display. Braun's VFD signal, Night Timetable's dot-matrix boards and Bench Scope's scope trace are each re-imagined, lit and scarce, while the rest of the page is grounded in a material (warm graphite, enamel on slate, blueprint paper, instrument grey).

The informed and carried entrants are well made but have converged on one slate-steel look. Evening Listing is the best finished of them, but a family would not tell it apart from Programme Guide. The mutants that only relight or retype (Flight Deck Lit, Signal Legend Relit, Reverse Video Reset, Drafted) are nearly identical to their parents at page scale.

Recurring lesson: the wild designs that won here did it with a governing rule that holds on every page ('every measure is a dial', 'every part is a numbered line', 'every plate is led by a figure'). Costume without such a rule (screws, hazard stripes, starfields, '80 COL') is where they lose points. For round 11, a crossover worth trying is Braun Signal's dials and warm faceplates with Night Timetable's Vera's-line Home structure, or Figure Ground's data figures on Braun's graphite.

scores.why: Yardstick. The components are consistent but generic: rounded cards everywhere, one green doing every job, no rules for 'here', read or act, and a monochrome glare. Its light (halo, bloom, pool) is the one thing worth keeping.

The most complete system on the panel. One listing drawing holds on Home, Ideas, To do, Status and Settings: a head column, a one-line row, a leader and tabular fact sub-columns ('2 h 10 min  S'). Steel reverse video marks 'here', denim links look like links, heads hold one line, and To do finally becomes one-line rows with the filter in the masthead. It loses a little on the repeated pewter L-bracket on every band and the empty head column on Ideas and To do, and its tube light is only partly restored (screen 0.8).

This answers the owner's latest word as a rule, not an effect: lit where the machine is live and matte everywhere the family keeps things. The instruments bloom and the lamps glow on dark slots, while plates, rows and bubbles stay flat. It also fixes Flight Deck's worst faults, since actions are keys again and setup items are rings, not checkboxes. The small mono-caps legends still sit below their rows in the hierarchy, Status is still plate-in-plate, and Next up now wraps 'Tuesday 29 / September'.

A disciplined graphic rule: a line is drawn only where there is an order. That gives the setup steps, the fortnight from a lit now-lamp, To do's due margin, Status's fallback chain, and Chat hanging from her screen to a lit ring at the box, where it is your turn. Kind-tinted idea cards bring grounded colour below the fold. A ring round every page icon and four tracks on Home push it towards diagram-everywhere.

Signal Legend's clear state system (rail legends, steel reverse video, square family surfaces and round glass) with a faithful tight-and-wide halo on the lit things. The lamp legend reaching every page is a real system rule. Moving the whole Chat to the left loses mine-versus-hers, which is a usability regression, and the glow on Vera's bubble edges starts to spread the light.

The strongest structure of round 9, and still sound. Its open faults are now fixed by its own child: heads wrap in the 10rem column ('Finish / setting up', 'The kids' / wishes'), head links in mono caps read as labels, and To do is two-line rows under a boxed filter.

Coherent rails, legends and reverse video, with the fortnight line and the due margin. The steel is so low in chroma that pages read grey, times sit far from their bubbles, and the Plex Bold titles are clunky.

A genuinely new layout rule: the machine gets one docked glass column (question, Next up, radar, spend tube) and the family's things lie on a square slate mat beside it. It works well on Home and Chat. It is let down by heavy saturated indigo keys used even for 'see more' (five head keys on Home) and by switched-off black under short columns on Plans, Status and Ideas. To do also has no column at all, which breaks the rule.

The only entrant to give the app a written type scale: six major-third steps, schoolbook a/g for the family's words, and a slashed zero for machine figures. That is worth adopting system-wide. On the page it is nearly identical to Reverse Video; legends and detail lines drop to 12.8px, and today on the month is still amber.
The drafting-pen callouts are invisible at page scale, and '80 COL / 25 LN' tells the family nothing, so they read as costume. The parent's wrapping heads and label-like links are untouched.

The best-argued colour code and square screwed faceplates. Actions and disclosures are set as caps legends, setup links are drawn as checkboxes, and the heads are smaller than their rows. Its lit child supersedes it.
Clear window grammar and reverse video. Double frames everywhere and loud legends set into the frame lines remain, and the amber 'today' on the month breaks amber's single job.

A tidy crossover: the lit greeting glass with an airglow, one cyan night-light with the single job of 'the way on', and numbered setup steps. The Newsreader titles are handsome but pull the page off the CRT. The coloured nav dots with no icons lose recognition, Status is plain, and Ideas shows few cards above the fold.

The most rigorous new system this round. Numbered chapters match the ruled bar, every part leads with a figure drawn from its own data (the Status wiring, To do's due timeline with a NOW line, the tally of kinds), paper reverse video marks 'here', and the tube warms up from a line. It drops the lit greeting pool, and every title as an underlined blue link is noisy. The all-caps mono buttons are harsh, some figures are decoration (the Plans key, Home's family tree repeating the counts), and the page is long and cold for a family.

Bold and legible wayfinding. Numbered enamel lines and Vera's line down Home are a real idea, and the Next up tube blooms like the original. But the colour load is high (five enamel colours, plus yellow, copper and green), a yellow 'here' rule tops the health page, and the setup panel carries a hazard stripe. The heavy weights read loud rather than calm, the greeting glass is gone, and Home's centre column leaves a dead lower half.

A coherent instrument panel whose scope draws the family's own data (Home's weeks as pulses with a rose trigger, the month on the glass). That is the best meaningful return of the phosphor. The one-size type rule shrinks the question to 15px, the grey plate greys the whole page, and the silver nameplates are the brightest non-green thing. Extended caps shout everywhere and the oxblood knobs flirt with red.

The constellation marks are charming and 'every row hangs from a round mark' is a rule. The centred column leaves half the desktop empty and the greeting loses its lit glass. Fraunces reads storybook, Status is one long column, and 27 of 56 targets are under 44px.

The dials and waveforms that draw real measures (drive times, the month, spend) are inventive. But the lifted warm-graphite ground (#161a17, surfaces #252320) greys and browns the black. Lowercase heads and buttons flatten the hierarchy, red means now, late and error at once, and 48 of 56 targets are small.
The keys and wells have good affordance, but the teal-tinted ground makes one blue-green family with the phosphor. The bands run Home long and 41 of 56 targets are small.
A single centred column with serif body text. It runs long, leaves the desktop half empty, loses icons in the nav, and has 45 small targets.

fixes.suggestion: Make this the standard, then finish its light and its frame. (1) Drop the pewter L-bracket that wraps every band and the masthead. One hairline top rule per band is enough, and the bracket reads as a repeated frame. (2) When a band's head column has nothing below the head (Ideas, To do), let the rows take the full width, or put the view switch and the count there, so there is no 230px of empty slate. (3) Bring the tube back to full: screenGlow 0.95-1.0, restore E1's two-layer halo on 'mind', E3's ring and pool on Send, and the tube's bloom, scanlines and power-on at the original values. Keep the page glow at 0.9 so the light stays scarce. (4) The row hover afterglow is invisible in the details strip, so give it a visible steel wash that fades over 900ms. (5) Write the seven type steps and the three rule weights as tokens in STYLE.md so Plans, Settings and the form inherit them.

Keep the lit-versus-matte rule. It is the clearest statement of 'light where attention belongs'. Set the plate legends in Plex Sans 600 at about .9rem sentence case, or in mono at least .8rem, so heads outrank their rows. Fix the Next up wrap by letting the tube text column take the width the radar leaves, or by stepping the date down one size. Flatten Status: rows sit directly on the plate with hairline dividers, and the inner boxes go. Carry the matte title tile and the lamp code onto To do, where nothing glows yet.

Keep 'a line only where there is an order'. Remove the ring round every page icon (keep rings only as stops on a line), cap Home at three tracks by making Lately added a plain list, and make sure the rails end at their last lamp. The kind-tinted idea cards are the round's best grounded colour below the fold, so breed them into the listing leaders.

The docked machine column is worth developing. (1) Make the column sticky and full-height on every page, holding one tube (Plans: Next up; Status: spend; Ideas: radar; To do: a count or now tube), so there is never switched-off black below it and To do follows the rule too. (2) Keys only for actions. 'All plans', 'All 4' and 'All 12' become underlined chalk links, and indigo stays on 'here', the tabs and the family's bubbles. (3) Lower the key indigo one step in chroma (#18243c), so it reads as cloth rather than a Bootstrap primary.

Keep the chapter numbering, the figure column and the data figures that carry meaning (the Status wiring, To do's due timeline with NOW, the kinds tally, the tube warming from a line). Fix the rest: (1) put the ask box back in a lit green-black glass pool, since the greeting's light is load-bearing; (2) row titles in ink with the underline on hover or focus only, and blue underlines kept for links in prose and for head links; (3) sentence-case buttons (Send, Add an idea); (4) drop decorative figures (the Plans legend key, the family tree repeating the counts) and collapse the column where a page has no real figure; (5) shorten Home by moving the tally figure beside To do rather than above it.

Keep the scope that draws the family's weeks, the frames with the name in the top line and the way on in the bottom line, and the lamps. Give the question its own step (1.8-2rem), keeping one size for everything else. Take the instrument-grey plate off the page so frames sit on the green-black. Swap the silver nameplate for a dark engraved pewter and the oxblood knobs for graphite, and set frame names in regular-width caps at .85rem, not extended.

Keep the numbered lines in the bar and on the phone tab bar, and Vera's line down Home. Cut the enamel colour to the disc and the one rule under each sign: no coloured title-plate tops and no coloured bar underline. 'Here' goes to steel, so yellow never tops Status. Replace the hazard stripe with a plain amber edge, step the head weights down one grade, and put the greeting back in lit glass.

Keep the dial and waveform monitors that plot real measures. Return the ground to green-black (#0b0e0c) with cool graphite surfaces, set heads and buttons in sentence case, give 'now' the brand lamp or steel so red means only failure, and restore 44px targets.

judges.notes: Through the design-system lens, the listing family has won the structure argument. Evening Listing is the first entrant whose single row drawing holds on every page in the sheets and plausibly on Plans, Settings and the form. It is the one I would write into the standard: bands with a head column, a one-line row, a leader, tabular fact sub-columns, steel reverse video for 'here', and denim underlined links. What the owner's latest word asks is the one thing it did not fully do, bring the original light back. Flight Deck, Lit shows the right way: one rule, lit versus matte, rather than a halo on everything. The best breed is Evening Listing's system with Flight Deck Lit's discipline on the tube, the lamps, Send and 'mind', each at the original's E1-E3 values (glow and screen both about 1.0 on those elements only). Signal Legend Relit's halo is faithful, but its glowing bubble edges show how quickly the light spreads to things that are not live. Reverse Video, Reset contributes the only written type scale, worth folding into the standard. The wild entrants each bring one strong idea and lose on basics. Figure Ground has the most rigorous new rule (a figure from each section's own data); Docked Terminal makes the machine a layout region; Bench Scope's data-drawn scope is the most meaningful phosphor. All three drop or shrink the lit greeting, and several lift or tint the ground or add a second loud hue (indigo keys, enamel rainbow, oxblood). Recurring checks: amber 'today' on the Reverse Video month, and 'here' in yellow or red on Status. Also small targets: Braun 48/56, Porcelain 45, Attract 41, Timetable 34, Figured Atlas 27 of about 56 on Home are under 44px.

scores.why: Yardstick. At a squint the page is green everywhere, so 'here', the one action and the content don't separate. 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px, and Coming up and To do sit as cards below 900px on a 2111px Home.

Best task page on the panel. The eye goes title, then Send, then Next up, then one-line rows read along a leader to tabular facts (Coming up, To do and Lately added all above 1300px; 8 Ideas rows above the fold). 0 targets under 44px. The steel reverse block for 'here' survives the squint, and every head link is an underlined sentence-case link with an arrow. It loses only on the light: the hover afterglow and power-on are barely visible.

Clearest wayfinding. Every destination is a numbered word in the bar, the paper reverse 'here' is the strongest in the squint, titles are big, every link is unmistakably an underlined link, and each figure sums up its section at a glance (5 plans, 12 ideas, 4 to do; late bars; Status's wiring of keys and connections). Costs: Home is 2437px of tall date tiles, 14 of 57 targets are under 44px, buttons are in mono caps, and the phone tabs lose their icons.

A real usability idea: the machine's glass column stays in view, so the ask box and Send are always within reach, with the family's desk beside it. Words are in the bar, the indigo latch reads clearly as 'here', Status gets a glance summary (WHO ANSWERS three lit, one off), it has 0 small targets, and the Tab order matches the visual order. Costs: 44px caps indigo keys for 'see more' compete with the primary, and on desktop Chat the composer sits top-left, away from the newest message at the bottom-right.

The most glanceable Home: 1385px in three columns, with the ask as the large centre hero. The numbered, enamel-coloured lines match the bar, the yellow arrow tiles plainly say 'go', and Chat's line ends at a lit ring by the box ('your turn'). Costs: 34 of 57 targets under 44px, the hazard-striped setup notice pulls the eye before the ask, 'here' is drawn two ways (a ringed coin, and a yellow tile on Status), and the phone tabs swap icons for loud number coins.

It fixes Flight Deck's worst fault: actions are buttons again and setup steps are rings, not checkboxes. The cyan outline reads clearly as 'here', and the light is back only on live things (tubes, lamps, Send). Costs: in Coming up and To do a caps date or name line sits above the title, so the eye meets metadata first; To do shows ISO dates.

Its lines carry order that helps comprehension: Chat hangs from her screen to a lit ring at the box, Coming up runs from a now lamp, and To do hangs its dues in a timetable margin with late ones in amber. Costs: 'here' is a faint steel cell with a tiny lamp that fades in the squint, Ideas is a tinted card grid (6 visible) rather than scannable rows, and Status is rows boxed inside plates.

The glow now points the eye (mind, Send, lit states), the steel reverse 'here' is clear, and Coming up runs as a track from a NOW lamp. But desktop Chat puts every line on the left, so who is speaking is no longer instant: a step back from its parent.
A clear state system (steel reverse, square ticks, rail links, dues in the To do margin) and Chat keeps the family's lines on the right. The steel is so quiet that sections blur together at a squint.

Excellent one-line rows and a tabular facts column, 0 small targets and a short Home. But the needle for 'here' disappears in the squint, the head links in mono caps read as labels, and 'Finish / setting up' wraps.

The parent's listing, plus numbered setup steps (a genuine comprehension gain) and leaders that tie each head to its rows. The '80 COL / 25 LN' dimensions tell the family nothing, and the parent's weak needle and caps head links remain.

Words in the bar, and cyan kept for the way on, so links read clearly. A large serif greeting title leads straight into the box and Send, and it has 0 small targets. 'Here' is a thin cyan cap with a star that fades in the squint, and Lately added and To do are card grids that are slower to scan than rows.

Reverse video for 'here' is clear, and the dialogs look like places to act. The legends are small mono caps in the frame lines, and the head links sit at the bottom-right of each window, away from the head the eye starts at. Today on the month is amber, which blurs amber's one job.

The type scale is tidier and the slashed zero helps figures, but the 12.8px legends now sit below 16px row titles, so section heads rank lower than their rows. Setup starters and detail lines shrink, and the page scale is otherwise unchanged.
A good colour code, but caps legends stand in for actions ('SAVE A THOUGHT FOR LATER'), setup links are drawn as checkboxes, and Status has seven full green bars, all of which slow understanding.

The dials read well as data (drive-time line, cost gauge), and Send has its own row on the phone. But 48 of 56 Home targets are under 44px, 'here' is a small dot beside a bold word, the phone tabs are dots without icons, the tube's segmented face is hard to read, and all-lowercase labels flatten the heads.

Lovely typesetting, and the constellation kind filter is a real aid. But Home places Coming up and To do at 1250-1800px on a 2831px page, half the desktop is empty, 27 of 56 targets are under 44px, and the small mono caps nav and buttons and the underline-and-dot 'here' are weak.

The trace of real plans is a fresh idea, and Home is compact. But one-size type shrinks page titles to a tiny nameplate, so the hierarchy is flat. A ticked box is drawn as an LED dot, and extended all-caps nav, buttons and legends slow reading.
Keys and wells are clear affordances, but 41 of 56 targets are under 44px, the latched tab reads backwards, and the bands spread Home thin.
Home is 2942px in one column, 45 of 56 targets are under 44px, the bar is small caps with dots, and small serif body text is thin on the dark ground.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the listing, the head column, the steel reverse 'here', the underlined sentence-case links and the 0 small targets. Bring the light back where it points the eye: a layered halo on 'mind', Send and the NOW lamp. Make the row-hover afterglow visible (a 2px sage edge fading over about 900ms; today it cannot be seen). On Ideas, move the All/Restaurants switch to just above the rows. Use the empty head column on Ideas and To do for the count and filter summary ('4 open, 2 late'). On To do, set 'No active reminder.' quieter, not repeated in mono beside every due date.

Keep the numbered chapters in the bar, the paper reverse 'here', the figure column that sums up each section, and the underlined blue links. Fix the controls: set Send, Filter and Add an idea in sentence-case sans, not mono caps, and pad the 'ALL PLANS' links, date tiles and title links to 44px. Shorten Home by setting each date as one line (1 Oct, Thu) so rows are about 48px, and fold figure 1.4 into the setup list. Keep the icons beside the numbers on the phone tabs. Under each phone thumbnail, print its one-line summary and put it in the Tab order. In Chat, add a speaker cue beyond shading (indent or right-align the family's lines). Let the lit figure glow like the original tube.

Keep the docked glass column, which stays in reach and is lit by the green pool, the slate desk and the indigo 'here' latch, and keep the Tab order that matches the visual order. Demote 'ALL PLANS →', 'ALL 4 →' and 'ALL 12 →' from 44px caps keys to underlined links with arrows, and keep keys for actions. On desktop Chat, dock the composer at the foot of the thread, where the eye lands after the newest line, and leave her header, READY lamp and the kids' conversations in the glass. Make the ask box three lines tall. Carry the glass the full height, or fill the dead black under short columns (Plans, Status) with lamps.

Keep the three-column Home with the ask as its hero, the numbered enamel lines that match the bar, the yellow arrow tiles and Chat's line that ends at the box. Raise the ALL tiles and title links to 44px targets. Move the setup notice below the ask, or fold it to one line, so the ask leads the eye and the Tab order. Draw 'here' one way everywhere, including Status's icon (drop the yellow tile). Put the icons back on the phone tabs, with the number as a small badge. Set Next up in the same tube face used elsewhere, not the fuzzy dot matrix. Indent or right-align the family's lines in Chat as well as tinting them copper.

Put the title first and the caps date or name line after it in Coming up, To do and Lately added rows, and set To do's due dates as relative words, not ISO. Keep the lit-versus-matte discipline and the action buttons.
Put the family's lines back on the right in desktop Chat, keeping the time rail, so the speaker reads at once. Keep the relit Send and mind and the NOW track.

Keep the scope that draws the family's own weeks. Bring back a real type scale (page titles about 2.2rem, heads about 1.3rem) and set the nameplate as a label beside the title, not instead of it. Draw a ticked box as a box. Set buttons and the nav in sentence case.
Keep the dials, which work as data. Raise the keys to 44px, draw 'here' as a filled cell rather than a dot, keep the icons in the phone tabs, and set the tubes in the readable mono face.
Put Coming up and To do above Lately added and setup. Above 64rem, split into two columns so the desktop isn't half empty. Set buttons and the nav in sentence-case sans at 44px.

judges.notes: Through this lens the panel has four structures that are genuinely better to use than today: Evening Listing's one-line rows, Figure Ground's chapters with a summary figure beside each part, Docked Terminal's always-reachable machine column and Night Timetable's three-column Home. Each changes the whole page content, not a corner. How well 'here' survives the squint, strongest first: Figure Ground's paper reverse; then the steel reverse of Evening Listing, Signal Legend and Reverse Video; then Docked Terminal's indigo latch; then Flight Deck's cyan outline; then Track Diagram's steel cell and Atlas's cyan cap; then the Programme Guide needle; and dots last (Braun Signal, Figured Atlas, Porcelain Atlas). Every carried and mutant entrant keeps 0 targets under 44px. Every wild entrant regresses there (Braun 48, Night Timetable 34, Figured Atlas 27, Figure Ground 14, Bench Scope 5), so a fix of target size should travel with any wild graft. Only Docked Terminal reorders the composer's Tab stops to match what is drawn (select, mic, Send, then the checkbox below). Recurring comprehension costs: mono-caps buttons and 'see more' links (Figure Ground, Bench Scope, Figured Atlas, Docked Terminal's keys); phone tabs that lose their icons (Braun Signal, Figure Ground, Figured Atlas, Night Timetable's coins); and desktop Chat transcripts that drop the family-on-the-right split (Signal Legend Relit, Night Timetable, Figure Ground, Braun Signal is fine). The best speaker and turn cue is the lit ring at the message box (Track Diagram, Night Timetable). The returning phosphor light helps this lens only where it marks the one action or the live thing (Flight Deck, Lit; Signal Legend Relit; Docked Terminal's glass). Evening Listing would gain most from taking that light on its Send, 'mind' and NOW lamp, and from a hover afterglow that can actually be seen. A strong next-round cross: Evening Listing's rows and steel reverse, with Figure Ground's summary figure in the head column and Docked Terminal's sticky ask.

scores.why: The yardstick. DM Sans everywhere, with mono only inside the tubes. Titles are heavy and tightly tracked, dates are proportional ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56'), there is no aligned facts column, and card grids give the page no typographic rhythm.

The most finished type system on the panel. It makes every fix the type lens asked of Programme Guide: heads hold one line, head links are sentence case, underlined and denim, and each fact has its own tabular sub-column (right-aligned date, then Plex Mono time, then relative day, as in '10:00 in 2 days'). Leaders run only where a fact follows, and VT323 field labels became Plex Mono caps. Small faults: Vera's date breaks over two lines in the greeting's head column, 'No active reminder.' is a sentence set in mono, and the head column is empty on Ideas and To do.

Clean rows: a big lining day numeral with small stacked OCT/THU caps, a semibold title over a proportional date line, and a mono relative day. The condensed Archivo heads are good. Against it: the see-more links are set as expanded-caps keys ('ALL PLANS →') that outshout the heads, the glass column squeezes the greeting's size and measure, and the VT323 'VERA TUESDAY…' line makes a fourth voice.

Real typesetting gains over today. Chat gives the date once and hangs each time at the end of a dotted leader to its bubble. To do hangs due times right-aligned in a mono margin. The fortnight sets large lining day numerals beside mono month and weekday. Archivo heads, DM Sans body and DM Mono facts pair cleanly. It loses a little on the two drawings of zero, the heavy card titles in the fortnight, and a Settings page still set as today's cards.

The purest type idea of the round: about forty sizes collapsed onto one major-third scale, and a slashed zero in every figure the machine reports, which is period-true and hard to misread. But it inverts the head-to-row order: 12.8px legends sit over 16px row titles. Secondary prose shrinks, the schoolbook a and g take away Plex's IBM character, and at page scale it looks almost identical to its parent.

Programme Guide's type intact, plus numbered balloons that make the setup steps a real sequence (a good device). The head wrap the lens flagged ('Finish / setting up') is still unfixed, the '80 COL / 25 LN' lettering is costume, and the head leaders add fine noise without adding order.

Newsreader display titles over Instrument Sans are handsome ('What's on your mind?' is the loveliest greeting on the panel), and the setup steps are numbered. But the serif carries section heads too, where it reads light and bookish and pulls the page off the CRT. It makes four voices with the tube face, and Lately added's two-column plates break the list rhythm.

Flight Deck's exact code, unchanged: label-over-data rows, Martian Mono caps legends set in the line breaks (now at a size that holds against the rows), and mono due stamps read straight down. The relit tubes give VT323 back its bloom. The mono due stamps wrap to two lines ('was due / 2 days ago'), and To do keeps ISO dates.

Signal Legend's Plex superfamily with its heads set into the rails, and the fortnight tiles in mono month over big numerals. The layered halo on 'mind' and the tubes brings back the lit word. Chat's times still sit in a far-left gutter, away from the bubbles, and the Plex Sans Bold titles remain a little blunt.

A written pixel scale (11.5, 13, 15, 19, 28-34) and Plex Mono for every readout show real discipline. But the Braun lowercase ('what's on your mind?', 'things to do', 'send', 'settings') is a mannerism: it flattens the hierarchy, starts sentences in lowercase, and sits oddly beside proper names. The body is still today's DM Sans.

One size for every word, ranked by weight, case, width and space, is a brave engraved-panel rule, and the Plex Mono readouts are crisp. In use, the expanded caps tracked at about .2em ('SAVE A THOUGHT FOR LATER', 'FINISH SETTING UP') shout, the greeting loses its display moment, and the squint shows no scale hierarchy at all.

The strongest new typographic personality: a stepped token scale, wide Archivo signage heads, condensed caps wayfinding labels, Doto dot-matrix on the departure boards (truly period), and Chat set as a timetable with bold tabular times and the date given once. Against it: heavy weights everywhere, narrow side columns that wrap titles ('Book the campsite at / Silver Falls'), and Doto grainy below board size.

An operator's manual set with conviction. A big Plex Sans Condensed greeting, numbered sections ('1.2 Coming up', '5.2 The list'), FIG. captions and mono tabular dates make a coherent superfamily system. It costs reading ease: buttons and disclosures are tracked mono caps ('EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE', 'SEND'), every row title is a blue underlined link, To do has ISO dates, there is an italic caption, and Home runs to 2437px.

The job split is right (Plex Sans for speech, Plex Mono for the catalogue), but Fraunces sets every name, from Status rows to centred Lately titles. It reads chunky and storybook on dark and pulls off the CRT for the sixth time. Spaced mono caps in the nav and a 2831px Home cost the rhythm.

Plex Sans with Plex Mono as one superfamily, legends knocked into the frame line, and right-aligned mono due times. It is coherent and period-true, but its mono-caps legends are loud, and its lists have no leader to an aligned facts column.

The Plex superfamily with each head set on its rail, and the fortnight tiles in tabular mono. The Plex Sans Bold titles are clunky, and Chat's times sit far from the bubbles. Its child, Relit, keeps all of this.

Still an excellent system: condensed Instrument Sans heads over text-width body, Plex Mono facts, and one-line rows read along a leader. Its heads wrap in the 10rem column, its head links are spaced caps, and 'in 2 days' shares a cell with the time. Evening Listing fixes all three.

An exact code: bone sans for data, grey Martian Mono caps for labels, and label-over-data rows with tabular due stamps. The caps legends in the line breaks remain its most distinctive and most debatable device.
Figtree with Martian Mono reads friendly but generic. There is no facts column or timetable, To do stays in cards as today, and the band heads rank the page by band rather than by type.
Fine book typesetting (a 45rem measure, generous leading, tracked caps labels), but serif body in controls and small text is thin on dark, and the single column runs long.

fixes.suggestion: Keep it as the base. (1) Keep Vera's date on one line in the greeting's head column: use white-space:nowrap with a shorter form ('Tue 29 Sep'), or put the name and date above the h1 below about 80rem. (2) Set 'No active reminder.' and other sentences in the sans at label size; keep mono for figures only. (3) Graft mut-1's written scale, but with a step at about .9rem so legends and heads never sit below the 1rem rows. (4) Graft Track Diagram's chat: give the date once as a dateline, then hang each time at its bubble. (5) Put something typographic in the empty head column on Ideas and To do (the count '12 ideas', a kind key, or the filter labels), or collapse it. (6) Per the owner's latest word, give 'mind' and the tube's VT323 lines mut-5's layered halo; the lit word is part of the type.

Keep the chat's date-once with times at the end of dotted leaders, and the hung due margin on To do; both belong in the standard. Draw zero one way across the facts. Drop the fortnight card titles to row size and weight so the day numerals lead. Carry the listing rows to Settings instead of today's cards.

The scale discipline is the idea to keep. Apply it to Evening Listing rather than Reverse Video, and add a .9rem step for legends and labels so heads never fall below rows. Keep the slashed zero for the machine's figures. Reconsider ss01/ss02: Plex's double-storey a is part of its IBM voice, and the schoolbook forms read softer and more SaaS.

Keep the stepped tokens, the numbered line signs, Doto on the boards and the timetable Chat. Lighten the weights (Archivo 600 for heads, 400-500 for rows and body). Use Doto only at board size, 20px and up. Widen the side columns, or stack to two columns, so titles do not wrap. Cap the condensed caps labels at about .06em tracking.

Keep the numbered sections, the FIG. captions and the big Plex Sans Condensed greeting: the most convincing manual typography yet. Set buttons and disclosures in sentence-case Plex Sans, set row titles in ink with a quiet underline rather than blue links, use relative due dates, and drop the italic caption. Shorten Home by putting two plates abreast at wide widths.
Keep the numbered balloons on the setup steps only. Fix the head wraps, as Evening Listing did (a 11.75rem column or text-wrap:balance). Drop the '80 COL / 25 LN' lettering and the head leaders.
Keep the body at one size, but allow two display steps: the greeting at about 2rem and the nameplate. Hold expanded-caps tracking at .08em or less, and set disclosures and actions in sentence case.
Keep the pixel scale and the Plex Mono readouts. Return titles, the greeting and buttons to sentence case; keep lowercase only for the small printed panel labels, where the Braun reference earns it.
If the serif stays, limit Newsreader to the greeting and page h1s. Set section heads and names in Instrument Sans, and keep the numbered setup steps.

judges.notes:
Through the type lens the tournament has converged on a standard, and Evening Listing is its most finished statement. It uses condensed Instrument Sans heads that hold one line, text-width sans for body, and Plex Mono for figures only, in fixed tabular sub-columns (date, then time, then relative day). Every list is a one-line row read along a leader that appears only where a fact follows. Links are sentence case, underlined and denim, and field labels are Plex Mono caps at about .72rem. Three typographic ideas from this round are worth adding to it:
(1) Reset's written scale. Collapsing about forty sizes to seven steps is exactly the 'type system with steps' the owner asked for. It needs one more step near .9rem so legends never rank below rows.
(2) The timetable Chat of Track Diagram and Night Timetable. The date is given once and each time hangs at its bubble, which answers the recurring 'time far from its bubble' fault.
(3) Figure Ground's numbered sections and captions, which prove a manual's apparatus can carry the period without paint.
Serif titles (Newsreader, Fraunces) and Braun lowercase remain handsome one-offs that pull off the CRT or lower the hierarchy. Expanded or tracked caps on buttons and disclosures faded again: Bench Scope, Figure Ground and Docked Terminal's keys. On the owner's latest word: the lit word is typographic too. 'mind' and the tube's VT323 read best with the layered halo that mut-4 and mut-5 restored, and Evening Listing (glow 0.9, screen 0.81) should take it. Remaining small faults to fix everywhere: mono used for sentences ('No active reminder.'), ISO dates on To do, and a greeting date breaking over two lines in a narrow head column.

scores.why: Yardstick. The controls are familiar and the page reads, but 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px, Home runs to 2111px, and bright green on black across the whole page is tiring at night. 'Here' is a faint pill and the lists are loose cards, so nothing can be read at a glance.

Every task is short on every page. Heads hold one line, links look like links (underlined denim with an arrow), 'here' is a steel block that survives a squint, the facts sit in true columns (27 min S, 10:00, in 2 days), and To do puts Show and Search in the page head. It has 0 small targets anywhere, 8 idea rows and the whole month above the fold, and Home is 1640px. Misses: the To do page cannot mark late tasks, there is dead slate in the head column on Ideas and To do, and Memory, Family and Status are still icons with no words.

The most 'where do I start' answer on the panel. I walked each task on each candidate's own pages.

**Send Vera a message.**
- Every candidate keeps the box first in the Tab order.
- Docked Terminal is best at "where do I start": the box stays docked beside the content on desktop, and on the phone the composer is pinned above the tab bar.
- Night Timetable makes the box the centre of Home.
- Bench Scope and Figured Atlas demote the question: it is 15px in Bench Scope, and in Figured Atlas the first screen is a centred column with half the desktop empty.

**See this weekend.**
- Best: Evening Listing and Programme Guide (one-line rows with a facts column), and Track Diagram, Signal Legend and Relit (the fortnight line).
- Worst: Figured Atlas and Porcelain Atlas, where Coming up is 1700px or more down the page.

**Tick a to-do and see what is overdue.** Every entrant but one marks late only on Home.
- Track Diagram's amber margin lamps and Flight Deck Lit's amber-framed tick boxes are the clearest.
- Figure Ground is the only one that marks LATE on the To do page itself. The rest say the view lacks `late`, so the one-line views.task_row change should ship with whichever design wins.

**Show only the restaurants.** It is weak wherever the switch is a legend set in a frame line (Reverse Video and its Reset: 12px caps). It is fine elsewhere.

**Find a date on Plans.**
- The month fits one screen in most entrants.
- It does not in Night Timetable, where the head plate pushes today's week to the fold.
- Braun Signal's red 'today' reads as an alarm.

**Consistency and focus.**
- The open select loses its green ring in Braun Signal, Bench Scope, Night Timetable and Figure Ground. That is round 6's bug, back again.
- Bench Scope draws a ticked box as a lamp dot, and Braun Signal and Figured Atlas draw ticks as round rings. All three break 'a control keeps the drawing people know'.

**Targets.** The slate family and Docked Terminal have 0 under 44px on every page. Braun Signal (48/56), the two Atlases (27-45/56) and Night Timetable (34/57) cost clicks and taps on the phone.

**Phone tab bar.** Icons are lost in Braun Signal, Figure Ground, Figured Atlas and Porcelain Atlas, and replaced by numbers in Night Timetable. That loses recognition.

**Nothing any design removed loses a family task.** The losses are affordance and legibility, not features.

**The owner's test.** On the heaviest test (change across the whole page), all of my top four change Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas, Status and To do, not just a corner. Docked Terminal changes the layout itself, and does it in a way that makes starting a message easier.

designs.name: Reverse Video, Reset
designs.tagline: Reverse Video set again: every word on the page on one major-third scale of six steps (a seventh for the tubes' figures), Plex Sans in its schoolbook a and g for the family's words, and the slashed zero of an IBM terminal in every figure the machine reports.
designs.concept: This is Reverse Video with only its type changed. The parent and the base stylesheet between them used about forty sizes, from .66rem to 2.9rem. Now every word sits on a major third (1.25) scale: .8, 1, 1.25, 1.5625, 1.953 and 2.441rem, plus 3.815rem used only for the tubes' big figures. Within a step, weight, case and colour do the ranking. The texture also splits by who is speaking. The family's words, set in Plex Sans, get its schoolbook single-storey a and g (ss01 and ss02), which reads rounder and more human. The machine's words, set in Plex Mono and in VT323 on the tubes, keep their engineered double-storey forms and take the slashed zero. The page should feel like the same calm old program, set more tidily: fewer sizes, clearer ranks and figures you can't misread.
designs.companions: None of the colours change; every token, glow number and colour role is the parent's. Steel reverse video marks "here", the family's surfaces are slate and steel, a cobalt wash sits in the greeting, sage is the lit colour, amber means "needs a look", and the exact #6dff9c stays on the mark, Send and the primary buttons, the word "mind", focus, the live lamps and the monitors. Type is the only thing that differs from the parent.
decisions: THE SCALE (major roll): ratio 1.25 on the 16px body, set as tokens --t-1 .8rem (12.8px), --t0 1rem, --t1 1.25rem, --t2 1.5625rem, --t3 1.953rem, --t4 2.441rem and --t6 3.815rem (tubes only). I chose 1.25 over 1.2 and 1.333 for three reasons. Its small step (12.8px) is almost exactly the .78rem the judges asked for on mono-caps legends. 1.333 would have left nothing between 12px and 16px for detail lines. 1.2's small step (13.3px) makes mono caps shout.

Each of the parent's sizes and every size in the base stylesheet (about 135 declarations) is assigned to a step by its job. t-1 is the small voice: labels, window legends, facts, times, said-by, tabs, detail lines, hints, tables, tags, date-leaf month and weekday, and the footer. t0 is for reading and doing: body, row titles, chat, fields, buttons, the bar's places and the month's day numbers. t1 heads a box: the summary of a details dialog, Settings card names, the restaurants line, the day on a date leaf and the tubes' small lines. t2 is for the month head, the greeting's question on desktop and the tube's base text. t3 is for titles on the phone, Sign in, and the tube headlines 'Pho Oregon' and '10 places'. t4 is the masthead, down from 2.9rem to 2.441rem, which also answers the note that Plex Bold at 3rem is clunky. A check script walked every visible text node on 25 pages at 1280px and 390px. Every size is on the scale, except Vera's glyph screens and the radar's range labels, which are aria-hidden pictures.

Titles step up at one breakpoint, 44rem: the masthead and h1 go from t3 to t4 and the greeting from t1 to t2. This replaces the parent's three fluid clamps. Tracking closes as size grows (t4 -.02em, t3 -.015em, t2 -.015 to -.018em, t1 -.008em) and small sans opens by .008em. Mono caps go from .07-.08em to .06em, as lessons.md asks. Leading is 1.5 for t-1 prose, 1.6 for body and chat, 1.3 at t1, 1.2 at t2 and 1.04-1.1 for titles.

Weights were tuned where a size moved. Window legends stay 600 at t-1 (from .88rem), so a legend outranks a 500 label of the same size by weight and heading colour, not size. Kind labels went from 500 at .875rem to 600 at .8rem, so 'Activity' and 'Restaurant' keep their presence. The date-leaf day went from 1.05rem to t1 (20px, 700, -.02em), and its month and weekday from .66rem to t-1. That brings the page's smallest words from 11.5px to 12.8px on every page.

STYLISTIC SET (minor roll): Plex Sans ss01 and ss02, the single-storey a and g, on all of the reading face: titles, rows, chat, fields and placeholders. I rendered each option before choosing. ss01 alone changes the texture most, since a is about 8% of English letters. Pairing it with ss02 keeps the forms consistent, the schoolbook pair a child learns to write, which suits a family's app. The mono is deliberately left with its double-storey forms, so the voice of the machine stays engineered.

SLASHED ZERO (minor roll): Plex Mono's default zero is dotted, so the `zero` feature gives the slashed form, the figure of an IBM terminal. It appears on every time, date, cost, id and fact ('10:00', 'in 10 days', '2026-09-27', '#10'). VT323 also has `zero`, so the change reaches the tubes too: '$0.00' in the spend readout and the 404 figure. The reading face keeps its plain zero.

HOW THE FEATURES ARE SET: the `font` shorthand resets font-feature-settings on every rule that uses it, and this Chromium ignores the @font-face feature descriptor (I tested both). So one rule, `*{font-feature-settings:var(--ot)!important}`, reads a per-face custom property: the root sets it to ss01,ss02, and each selector that sets a mono or terminal face sets it to zero. The check script confirmed each text node gets its face's features on every page, with two exceptions reset to sans: the people facts and the amber 'Finish setting up' legend.

Nearest versions where the scale hurt. The starters ('What should we do this weekend?') wrapped to two lines at t0, so they are t-1 with 1rem padding and fit one line on desktop. The Settings side menu wrapped 'Personality and family' at t0, so it is t-1, as secondary navigation like the tabs. The bar's own menu stays t0. 'any but dropped' wrapped inside its select, so filter selects are nowrap. A crumb link that was sans .92rem beside mono crumbs now takes the crumbs' face and step (`font:inherit`, line-height 1.3), which keeps the 44px target. `code` is 1em, because Plex Mono and Plex Sans share an x-height and the old .88em shrink was for DM Mono.

Only type changed. The markup is the parent's, copied unchanged to variants/r10-mut-1, and no template edit was needed. Colours, layout, frames, glows and motion are untouched. The only non-type changes serve the new sizes: the starters' padding, the filter selects' nowrap, and inline hit padding on one-word links in the small voice, so Settings, the form and General keep 0 targets under 44px. Legend icons went from 1.05rem to 1rem, onto the grid.
designs.measures: Final full render (./check.sh palettes/r10-mut-1.json): 0 hard checks failed and 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 12.37 and brand_on_bg 15.18, both the parent's. Green share of colour: home 29.2%, ideas 53.8%, chat 34.0%, status 19.9%. Hue entropy: home .655, ideas .638, chat .641, status .625. Kinds dE (typical / deuteranopia / protanopia): 13.6 / 5.5 / 7.4, closest pair restaurant~activity. Sections dE: 13.4 / 5.5 / 5.2. Smallest text is 12.8px on every page (parent 11.52). No sideways scroll anywhere. 0 targets under 44px on every page (Home 0/56, To do 0/97). Greeting's top-right corner pixel at (1150,120) samples (26,33,48), as the parent. At (100,640) the pixel is (19,22,18), but that point falls just below the greeting. The glow itself, at (100,540), samples (34,54,40), as the parent. Home is 1678px tall (parent 1675). The type check script, at 1280px and 390px across 25 pages, found every visible size on the seven steps and every text node carrying its face's features.
strengths: A real type system you can state in one line: a 1.25 scale with six steps plus a display step for the tubes, down from about forty sizes, applied to every page including Plans, To do, Settings, the forms, Family, Wishes and Memory, not only the sheets.

It fixes Reverse Video's recorded type faults. The legends that shouted at .88rem are now 12.8px at .06em, close to the judges' ask of .78rem and .08em. The 2.9rem Plex Bold masthead is now a calmer 2.441rem.
The smallest words on every page go from 11.5px to 12.8px, and the date leaf's month and weekday go from 10.6px to 12.8px.

The slashed zero makes every figure unmistakable and period-true ('10:00', '2026-09-27', '$0.00' on the tube). The single-storey a and g give the family's words a warmer, rounder texture than the engineered mono. So the face itself now tells the family's voice from the machine's.
Ranks within a step come from weight, case and colour: the 600 heading-colour legend over the 500 label colour, the 600 title over the ink-2 detail. That is the discipline a coherent standard needs.
Nothing else moved: colour, markup, layout, targets (0 under 44px) and the signature are all the parent's, so the judges can see what type alone does.
weaknesses: Detail lines went from 14px to 12.8px, and so did Family's four-line intro and the Settings card state lines, because the scale has nothing between 12.8 and 16. They read well but are a step smaller than the parent's, and long secondary prose is the worst hit.
