designs.name: Programme Guide, Drafted
designs.tagline: The same listing on slate, now drawn like a service manual: every head a callout led to its rows, every monitor dimensioned, the setup steps a numbered sequence, and a ruled mark between the parts.
designs.concept: This is Programme Guide with only its graphics redrawn, in the way a 1980s service manual draws its figures. One fine pewter-denim pen does all of it: a 1px line, slim filled arrowheads, a dot where a leader touches the thing it names, and small Plex Mono lettering. The listing reads as a technical sheet. Each part's head points at its rows, each monitor carries its measurements, and the setup steps are numbered like an assembly sequence. The #6dff9c phosphor still lights only what is live.
designs.companions: The companions are the parent's own, unchanged. The one addition is a drafting pen in the parent's denim family. Lines are #4a5a6c, terminators, arrowheads and the registration mark are #7389a6, and lettering is #8b9bb0. All three sit between the parent's --rule #2d353b and --needle #84a0c4, so the drawing reads as blueprint ink on slate, not as a new colour. The pen goes on the dividers, head leaders, monitor dimensions, title-tile crop marks and step connectors. The setup band keeps its amber: its divider is drawn in the parent's #7a5d31, with an amber registration mark (#b08440), and the step balloons are amber-ringed with people-amber numerals. Green is untouched.
decisions: MAJOR, schematic language, heads: every band head (h2 in the head column, and the floated panel heads on settings pages) becomes a callout. A hairline leader runs from the name across the 1.75rem gutter and ends in a 5px dot where it touches the rows it names (desktop, 64rem and up, where the head column exists). The heads' icons and the page-title icons are drawn in the same fine pen (stroke 1.35 against 1.75), done in CSS so the rows and the bar keep the parent's icons. The icon sprite is not redrawn, because the roll did not reach the rows or the bar.

MAJOR, schematic language, monitors: the crt macro in _ui.html now draws an aria-hidden spec on every monitor (Next up, the Ideas radar, the Status spend readout, Sign in, 404, 403). It has two dimension lines outside the case, each with extension lines, arrowheads and broken-line lettering: the tube's width, '80 COL', below, and its height, '25 LN', at the right. Those are the IBM 5151's text geometry, so the lettering is period-true rather than invented. There is no callout balloon on the power light: every placement I tried crossed an extension line or needed room the page does not have. Two dimensions, the same on every monitor, was the cleaner system.

MAJOR, schematic language, setup steps: Home's 'Finish setting up' rows swap the parent's amber rings for numbered callout balloons (CSS counters, 1.6rem, amber ring, mono numerals), joined by one pewter line. That is a line carrying sequence, which the panel rewarded in round 9. For the system, the same balloons and connector are written for the /setup overview (.setup-list .number), the setup progress bar's unchosen steps, and the steps to get a key (ol.steps). The current setup step keeps the parent's lit green. The screenshots do not reach those pages.

MINOR, drawn divider: every part's top rule (bands, the Settings layout, the People panel, the chat thread, and a page head that stands alone) is redrawn as a measured span. It is a hairline whose ends turn down 6px like a bracket, with a 15px registration mark at the column stop, where the head column meets the listing. On the phone the mark sits over the designator column, and in the chat thread over the gutter between names and bubbles. I chose a registration mark because it belongs to both drafting and printing, which fits the owner's interest in typesetting.

One divider, not two: the parent drew both a page-head rule and a band-top rule about 22px apart. With marks on both they read as a stutter, which round 7 already called out. Where a band follows the page head, only the band's drawn rule remains. Where the head stands alone (the new-idea form), the head keeps its divider, flipped so its bracket ends turn up toward the head.

Title tiles: the page's own figure (Ideas, To do, Plans, Status, Settings, General, New idea) is set in eight crop marks, like a detail on a drawing sheet. Vera's screen tile is left alone: it clips its overflow, so crop marks would not show.

Where a picture needed room. (1) Next up, Ideas' radar and the Status readout get 1.15rem below the case for the width dimension, so Ideas' list starts about 13px lower. (2) Next up gets .6rem at its right for the height dimension. That amount was measured so 'Tuesday 29 September,' still sets on one line: 1.1rem broke it onto three lines, so I went back. (3) The Sign in monitor's bottom margin grows from 1.75rem to 2.6rem, so the dimension does not crowd the title. On the phone, Next up shows only the width dimension, because the welcome's .75rem padding has no room for the height.

Nothing else changed: tokens, glow numbers, faces, type steps and layout are the parent's, and all the drawing CSS is appended after the parent's (6.7k characters). There is a forced-colours fallback that brings the plain rules back and hides the drawings. Assets are in variants/r10-mut-2/static: draft-reg.svg, draft-reg-amber.svg, draft-arrow-l/r/u/d.svg and draft-dot.svg. They use presentation attributes only, with no style element and no script. The source CSS is kept, with comments, in variants/r10-mut-2/drafted.css.

Smallest text 11.52px, no sideways scroll, 0 of 56 Home targets under 44px, and 3.7% of Home's words differ, the same as the parent: all drawing lettering is aria-hidden or generated. removed.txt is empty.
strengths: One pen, one set of terminators and one lettering style across dividers, head leaders, monitor dimensions, crop marks and step balloons. It reads as a coherent drafting system, not scattered effects, and it reaches Plans, To do, Settings and General through CSS as well as the pages in the sheets.
The head callouts carry meaning: each name visibly points at what it labels, which ties Programme Guide's head column to its listing across the gutter.

The setup steps are now a readable numbered sequence joined by one line, the kind of line the panel has rewarded because it carries order. The same balloons are written for the /setup pages and the steps to get a key.

Sign in, 404 and Status are the pages that have always been dominated by the monitor. Their monitors now read as a figure in a manual ('80 COL' by '25 LN', the IBM 5151's text geometry) and are more than a green slab, with no added glow.
Restraint: no colour, face or layout change, no added green, no ring round every icon. The page-head and band double rule became a single drawn divider, which removes a stutter the parent had.
weaknesses: Viewed at a squint, the page is still Programme Guide. Hairlines in a quiet pewter do not change mass or colour, so the owner's 'difference at a glance' is carried by detail, not by tone.
The phone's first screen is almost identical to the parent. Next up's width dimension sits under the tab bar, the height dimension is dropped for lack of room, and the phone has no head leaders.

The monitor dimensions are decoration: '80 COL' and '25 LN' tell the family nothing, and a skeptic may call them costume. They also cost a little room: Ideas' list starts about 13px lower, and the Next up and Status monitors are about 18px shorter.

Heads that wrap to two lines ('Finish setting up', 'The kids' conversations') get a short leader floating between their lines. Its negative margin also lets 'The kids' wishes' run about 5px past the head column instead of wrapping.

Chat and To do change least: one drawn divider, one leader on the kids' band, and on To do only the divider and the tile's crop marks, because those pages have no heads, monitors or steps for the roll to draw on.
The setup-page and key-step balloons are written but not shown in any screenshot, so they are unverified in a render.

designs.name: Atlas After Hours
designs.tagline: A star atlas set as a book and read after closing by an arcade's night light: graphite plates in a two-page spread, Newsreader titles over a grotesque, a disc for each part and a star for the page you are on, and the phosphor only where a screen is running or you act.
designs.concept: The atlas is opened as a spread. Newsreader names the pages and sections, a disc in its star colour hangs in the margin beside each part, an eight-rayed star marks the page you are on, and the green airglow rises off the horizon at the foot of the lit greeting glass. The arcade supplies the room: graphite cabinets as plates, a dark deck for the bar and the colophon, sunk wells to type into, keys with a little travel, and one cyan night light that shows the way on. It should feel quiet, typeset and a little after hours, with #6dff9c lit only where the machine is live or where you act.
designs.companions: One companion, the night light, cyan #7dccdf (OKLCH 0.80/0.082/h215). It is Attract Mode's teal turned 20 degrees cooler, so it leaves the green family. In this revision it has exactly one job, the way on, here and light: every head link ('All plans →', 'Add an idea', 'Change a key'), the Vera/Home disc and star in the bar, the Home pill, the 2px cap on the family's bubbles, the current Settings item's edge, the star and head discs on Home, Vera, Status and Settings, the zenith at the top of each page, and the greeting's far corner (a bluer rgb(104 178 240) at 0.14 that samples (25,42,49)). The neutrals that shared its hue are now plain. Label is #a3afb0 (C .014, 15 dE from the night light) and key text #c3cdce, so 'FROM', 'SEARCH' and the starters no longer read as faint links. The plate edge is #2d393d (C .017) in palette.css and card-edge. The grounded solids are graphite with a breath of cool (surface #162023, lines #243033/#314043) over a green-black ground #0d1411, with the deck #080f0d under the bar and the foot. The soft arcade section colours stay on the discs, kind labels, 30% section rules and calendar slips: periwinkle plans #84b7f8, lilac ideas, lemon to-do, apricot people, pink wishes. Each colour now has one drawing. Apricot is caution alone: the setup panel's edge and its step numbers, 'was due', 'Needs a look', plus its own restaurant disc and eyebrow, and no other box is edged in it. Mint #76d8aa is ticks, done and the box being typed in. #6dff9c is the mark and caret, Send and the one primary per page, 'mind', focus, the live lamps and the tubes.
decisions: STRUCTURE from Porcelain Atlas: Newsreader for h1, section h2s and the greeting question; magnitude marks (a disc per part and per kind, the eight-rayed clip-path star before every page title and for the current bar item); section rules tinted 30% in each part's colour; star-catalogue dates (a large DM Mono day with month and weekday stacked beside it); ruled catalogue lists; square 2px family surfaces with hairline edges; the Settings index as a table of contents; airglow on the horizon; a centred colophon; words, not icons, in the desktop bar.

COLOUR and MATERIAL from Attract Mode: every token role and glow number (glow 0.49, screenGlow 0.82, topGlow 0.7, washGlow 1.0, ambientGlow 0.9, quietFilter); wells with a shadowed top edge; keys with a 1px lip that press down 1-2px; the deck under the bar and the foot; the roll bar that runs down each tube as it switches on (one-shot, off under reduced motion).

RECONCILED from the structure parent, each a round-9 fix: the lit glass greeting with Next up beside it; a two-page spread at 60rem and wider (Coming up and To do on the left page, Lately added and the kids' wishes on the facing page); the serif kept to titles, with Instrument Sans for reading and pressing and DM Mono tabular slashed-zero figures; sentence-case nav, tabs and buttons; icons on the phone tabs, buttons and head links; the 2px #6dff9c focus ring; the starfield dropped.

firstDraft.name: Signal Legend Relit
firstDraft.concept: Signal Legend exactly as it was: slate trays with their heads set into the rails, steel reverse video for "this one", square family surfaces and round machine glass. The one change is that its phosphor gives off light again the way a green-screen tube did. Wherever the machine is lit (the mark and cursor, "mind", Send, the box being typed in, the lamps, the NOW dot, her screens, the monitors, her newest line), there is now a tight bloom inside a wide faint halo. Everything that lights up does so at once and fades over 1.2s. The rest of the page stays grounded and quiet, so the light reads as the machine switched on, not as glare.

designs.name: Braun Signal
designs.tagline: Quiet grey hardware with one green key: every page a faceplate, every measure a dial, the phosphor kept for the displays that show a signal.
designs.concept: FamilyDB as a piece of Rams-era hi-fi. Warm graphite faceplates printed with small lowercase labels sit on a green-black case. The phosphor green is kept for the display windows, the one green key, focus and the live lights. Every measure (what is coming, how far places are, the month, the day's spend) is read off a linear dial with a signal on it, and one red needle marks "now". It should feel calm, tactile and exact: a machine that is on and listening, not a Matrix screen.
designs.companions: Needle red #f76d89 (OKLCH hue 10, lightened from #ef617f so it reads 4.63:1 on the lightest plate) is now the page's only red, because --danger and --needle are merged. It appears in two forms. As a line or as print it means "now" or "late": the needle on time dials, the "now" scale word, today's calendar cell and date counter, the "today" tag on the Next up glass, late tasks and the late segments of the to-do meter. As a filled plate it means something went wrong: the error dot, the danger key, a failed light in Needs attention, and the red Status tile. Warm graphite neutrals (hue about 88) carry the surfaces, lines and ink. The section and kind colours are grounded pastels, used only as small solid keys: ideas lilac #ac9be0, plans steel blue #85c8e6, to do ochre #e6db83, family and restaurants amber #ef9f5f (also the "needs a look" lights and half-lit status lights), wishes rose #f0b4ca, seasonal terracotta #e57f6f, outing leaf #80cd82. Sage #9fd3a9 is the accent for Home, Vera, Status and Settings. Lit #8cdda2 is the calmer green for switches, meters and the box being typed in. Brand #6dff9c stays exact for the mark and its caret, the primary key, focus, live LEDs, the word "mind" and the listening mic.
decisions: A clean sheet (variants/r10-wild-1/sheet.css, 87.6 KB) with a written standard at the top in six parts, each with one job: faceplates, keys, lights, labels, displays and colour keys. The header also sets down the type scale and the one-red rule, so the standard carries to any page.

Type has five steps and no others: --t-label 11.5, --t-meta 13, --t-body 15, --t-head 19 and --t-title 34 (28 on a phone). Every size in the sheet was mapped onto these, replacing nine sizes between 11.5 and 16px. Section and panel heads are now 19px/600 at -0.012em, so 'coming up', 'to do' and 'lately added' stand clearly above their rows. Doto stays on the displays with its own scale. Inter's opsz is set to 32 on titles. Tabular figures are used on every time, date counter, relative tag, count and id.

One dial macro in _ui.html is used on every display. It is drawn in real pixels with no viewBox, and each mark sits at its percentage of the width, so the scale words are 11.5px mono on every screen and strokes are 1px. Scales are linear. Home runs 0 to 28 days, with a tick a day and majors at now, 1w, 2w, 3w and 4w; it reads each plan's days back exactly from views.RADAR_RINGS. Ideas runs from home out to the furthest place rounded up to the hour, with a tick every quarter hour, and the caption now says '3 h'. Plans covers the grid's visible days, 31 Aug to 4 Oct, with Mondays printed and a month name only on days outside the month shown.

The needle is kept to its one job. It stands at now on the time dials (Home, Plans, 404) and nowhere else. Ideas has no needle, since distance is not time; the nearest place's burst is simply the brightest. Relative tags on the glass are quiet phosphor outlines, and only Home's 'today' turns red. Plans dims the signal and bursts before today and lights them after.

Plans puts the month in its head. The display is a slim 68px strip, with the month in Doto and '1 day with plans' at the left and the dial across the rest. The earlier and later keys run the full height at its two ends. The list/month keys sit in the page head on both Plans views, so switching never moves them. The weeks already gone shrink to 52px rows with faint figures, so today's week and its plans are on the first screen.

To do gets the system. A 12-segment LED meter sits at the right end of the head's signal line. Each row is a listing: the round key, the title, and the number printed at the right in faint mono. Under the title come who and the due time in words ('due sun 27 sep, 19:56', in mono with tabular figures), then the reminder state. The status tag only shows when it differs from the filter. The template, meter and CSS for late rows (a red date and a red edge on the key) are ready for row.late.

Chat is a 3:2 two-track tape: Vera's track is wider, the tape is 56px, and there is 20px of air between a line and its mark. Each time is printed on the tape under the mark as a two-line mono counter, and the text is capped at 60ch. On a phone it folds to one track and the time goes back into the line.

Every key and field is --hit tall: 40px under a mouse and 44px on a phone. This covers nav keys, starters, tabs, filter fields, inline actions, menu and settings-nav rows, and wish actions. The task key is a 26px grey disc inside a 40px target. Idea rows are clickable across their whole width.

Lowercase is now a written rule rather than a transform on everything. It applies to labels the app names. Names, acronyms, sentences and the family's words keep their case, through .name, <abbr> and a words() macro used in page titles, crumbs, the settings menu, the settings nav and the settings cards. So 'AI model', 'what Vera remembers', 'sign in to FamilyDB', 'Vera' in the bar and a message's own title keep their case. The mark and the footer print 'FamilyDB', and the starters are shown the way ask.js will write them. Switch labels such as 'Send where I am' are sentences and keep theirs.

The grid holds to the pixel: `scrollbar-gutter: stable` keeps main's left edge at 91px on every page. Ideas' tabs sit inside the one control faceplate with their own printed 'list' label, behind a rule, and all controls share one height and one baseline.

Lights: 'not set up' is a hollow ring in the edge grey, amber half-lit means 'needs a look', and red only fills when something has failed. The VU meter is drawn at a fixed 240px, so its scale prints at 11.5px, and its lines stay 1px.

Kept from the draft: warm graphite on a green-black case, the section head's burst delimiter, Vera drawn as her voice, the ask box as hardware with its input-level trace, the sign-in grille, the 404 flat line, colour as small solid keys, the base-select picker with a lit dot, the lit switch, the 2px brand focus ring, Inter with IBM Plex Mono, and the dotted grille above the footer.
designs.measures: Final full render (./check.sh palettes/r10-wild-1.json): 0 hard checks failed and 1 guideline missed (words: lost 8.7%, unchanged from the draft). ink_on_bg 13.7:1, brand_on_bg 13.76:1, danger/needle text on surface-3 4.63:1. Green share of colour and hue entropy by page: home 22.9% and 0.686, ideas 53.6% and 0.707, chat 28.0% and 0.588, status 9.6% and 0.634. Bright green per mille: home 2.99, ideas 5.35, chat 3.91, status 0.44. Kinds ΔE typical/deutan/protan: 17.0 / 6.0 / 6.5. Sections ΔE: 19.4 / 7.1 / 7.8. Smallest text is 11.5px on every page. No sideways scroll anywhere. Words differing: home 3.7% (the conversation glance had aged out of RECENT, which is not the design), ideas 3.0% (new caption), plans 2.5%, to do 0.7% (the redundant 'open' tags), lost 8.7%, and 0% on every other page. Targets under 44px on desktop: home 48 of 56 (they are now 40px; on a phone they are 44px). Greeting corner pixels: (1150,120) = (41,39,36) and (100,640) = (37,35,32), the console faceplate's warm graphite with no wash.
strengths: A coherent, written standard: six parts with one job each, five type steps, one red with two stated forms, and --hit for every control. It holds on Plans, To do, Settings, Status, Memory, Family and the idea page, not only Home.
The dials are now exact: linear scales, scale words at the page's label size on every screen, 1px lines, and the needle only at now.
Plans is transformed. The month is a 68px strip in the head, the past weeks fold away, and today's week with its three plans is on the first screen.
The difference from today shows on every page at a glance: warm graphite hardware, green only where there is a signal, small colour keys and a real type hierarchy.
Chat reads like a tape, with counters on it and a wider track for Vera's longer answers.
Casing is principled: 'AI model', 'what Vera remembers', 'FamilyDB' and 'Vera' in the bar keep their case, while printed labels stay lowercase.
weaknesses: To do still shows no late marks. The template cannot know the time: views.task_row passes no `late` and no clock reaches the page. The late CSS, the red edge on the key and the red meter segments are wired to row.late and wait on that one-line views change. Until then the To do meter shows only the open count, while Home's shows 2 late in red, and the two pages disagree.

Some of the dial arithmetic lives in templates because views.py is out of reach. Home reads days back from radar blips via a copy of RADAR_RINGS. Ideas parses each row's drive time from its English words ('about 2 h 10 min ...'). Due weekdays are computed with Sakamoto's method. It is exact today but fragile if views' wording or the ring table changes. In the repository it belongs in a views.dial helper.
Desktop targets are 40px, not 44px, so the health count of targets under 44px barely moves (home 48 of 56). Inline text links (setup steps, plan titles) remain under 24px.
Calendar event edges are all steel blue, not kind-coloured: the month's entries carry no kind.

Seven more templates are overridden (tasks, plans, settings, settings_section, memory, activity, settings/messages), several only to keep a name or acronym in its case inside a lowercase label. Each is a maintenance cost.
'from' (lowercase field label) still sits beside 'Send where I am' (a sentence), by the stated rule. Someone may still read it as a clash.
The due time in Plex Mono at 13px reads a touch louder than the Inter meta beside it.
revisions: Needle red kept to its one job. `.crt .rel` is now a quiet phosphor outline; only `.rel.now` and `.rel.late` are red, and Home adds `now` to 'today'. Ideas has no needle; the nearest burst is the brightest. `.light.off` is a hollow ring in var(--edge), and a new `.light.bad` (a filled red plate) is used only in Needs attention. --danger and --needle are merged into one red, #f76d89, lightened from #ef617f so it passes 4.5:1 on surface-3 (it was 4.13). The line or print form means now or late; the filled plate means a failure.

The dials were rebuilt as one real-pixel `dial()` macro (the critic's views.dial, done in _ui.html because views.py is out of reach), with `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` and every scale word at 11.5px mono. Home runs 0 to 28 days with equal weekly majors and each plan placed by its exact days away. Ideas runs from 0 to the furthest place rounded up to the hour, and its caption follows. Plans covers the grid's visible days. The Status VU is fixed at 240px so its labels print at 11.5px. `.next-title` uses Doto wght 900 and ROND 100 with text-wrap: balance, a 2-line clamp and a clamp(22px, 1.2vw + 12px, 28px) size. `.next-up` has `align-self: start`.

Plans: the display is folded into a 68px strip under the head, with the earlier and later keys as its full-height ends. The list/month keys moved into the head on both Plans views (plans.html is now overridden too). Past weeks are 52px with faint figures (`tr:has(~ tr td.today)`), and the redundant month-display band is gone.

To do: the page is overridden. It gets the LED meter on the head's signal line, listing rows with the number at the right, due times in words and in mono with tabular figures, the status tag hidden when it matches the filter, and 'No active reminder.' moved inline. The late styling is prepared for row.late. Actually adding `late` to views.task_row was not possible from here.

Type: five steps (--t-label, --t-meta, --t-body, --t-head, --t-title), and every rule is mapped to one of them. Section and panel heads are 19px/1.2/600 at -0.012em. The chip month and weekday went from 10.5 to 11.5px. Tabular figures are on every time, date, count, id and tag.

Grid: `html { scrollbar-gutter: stable }`. Ideas' tabs are moved inside the filter faceplate with a printed 'list' label and a rule, all at one control height; on a phone the rule turns into a bottom border.

Lowercase is written down as a rule with its boundary in the sheet header. The transform is off the mark, the footer mark and the starters. A words() macro keeps acronyms (in <abbr>), names after the first word and whole sentences in their case; it is used in page titles, crumbs, the settings menu, the settings nav and the settings cards. Vera's name in the bar, 'Continue with Vera', 'sign in to FamilyDB', and names in memory, activity and message-settings labels keep their case.

Chat: tracks are `minmax(0,3fr) 56px minmax(0,2fr)` with an 8px column gap (about 20px between a bubble and its mark), the tape line is computed to the new centre, and text is capped at 60ch. Times moved onto the tape as 11.5px mono counters, following the critic's optional suggestion.

Hand-size keys: --hit is 40px (44px on a phone) for nav keys, starters, tabs, fields, filter keys, inline actions, menu rows, settings-nav rows and wish actions. The task key is now a 26px disc in a 40px target. Idea track rows are whole-row links. Phone fields are 16px so iOS does not zoom.
Smaller fixes: the idea page's 'drop it' key no longer sits 8px low; the 403 page keeps working through a `radar` wrapper around the new dial.

Declined: kind-coloured calendar event edges, because entry_row carries no kind (the month page's data has none). Declined: the needle at 'home' on Ideas; I dropped it instead, because 'here' is not 'now' and a needle there would reintroduce red with no job. Declined in part: 44px keys on desktop; I kept 40px for mouse use and 44px on a phone.
crit: Keep the needle red to its one job. Now it leaks in three places. (1) `.crt .rel` (sheet.css ~l.892) paints every relative tag red, so the Ideas display shows the distances "18 min NW" and "2 h 45 min W" as red chips. (2) The Ideas dial parks the needle on the nearest place (radar() with b.next). (3) `.light.off` (l.1540) rings every "no key / not configured" light in needle red, so Status shows seven red rings on a healthy install, against the sheet's own legend ("hollow off"). Fixes: make `.crt .rel` a --phos-dim outline by default, and red only with a `.now`/`.late` class the template adds (Home's "today"). On Ideas, put the needle at "home" (you are here) or drop it and let `.burst.next` mark the nearest place. Use `.light.off { background:none; border:1.5px solid var(--edge) }`, amber `.part` for "needs a look", red only for failures. Also merge --danger #f66e60 into --needle #ef617f, or draw danger differently (a filled plate against the needle's line): as they stand they read as the same red.

Make the dials exact and print their scales at one size. `.dial-label` is 10px inside a 400-unit viewBox, so the scale words come out at ~8.6px on Home's Next up, ~6px on home-phone, ~10px on Plans and ~14px on Ideas. `.vu-label` is 9.5px and `.vu-unit` 8.5px. Draw the scale words as HTML spans under the SVG (`left: X%`, `font: 500 11.5px/1 var(--num)`) and give strokes `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`. Make the scales linear, or honestly labelled. Home: days 0-28 with day minors and equal weekly majors (now, 1w, 2w, 3w, 4w), each plan placed by days away rather than by the radar radius worked back through `**` (_ui.html radar macro l.151-175). Ideas: 0 up to the furthest place, rounded (0, 1 h, 2 h, 3 h), so 2 h 45 isn't clamped at "2h" under a caption that says "2 h at the right". Plans: the scale should cover the grid's visible days (31 Aug to 4 Oct) so the trailing week's plans show. Move all of this into a `views.dial(points, span, marks)` helper. For `.next-title` Doto, set "wght" 900 and ROND up, `text-wrap: balance`, a 2-line clamp and `font-size: clamp(22px, 1.2vw + 12px, 28px)`. Set `.next-up { align-self: start }` so a tall left column leaves no empty glass.

Plans: fold the display into the head. The month display (plans_month.html .crt) is a ~170px band that repeats "1 day with plans". With every past week at full height, today's row (29, red edge) sits at y≈883 and no plan is visible on the first screen. Make it a slim strip, 72px at most (Doto month on the left, dial on the right), with earlier/later as the keys at its two ends in the head's row. Give the weeks before today's `min-height: 56px` and `--faint` numerals (a `past` class, or `tr:has(~ tr td.today)`). Today's week and the next then sit above the fold, and the kind-coloured event edges read at first glance.

To do: carry the system. It is the one page with no instrument and no late mark, and every row of a list already filtered to Open wears an ochre `.tag.status-open`. "#4 · Call the dentist" and "Due 2026-09-27 19:56" read like a debug listing next to Home's to do. Add `late` to `views.task_row` (due_at < now, one line). Mark late rows with `.late` in needle red on the due span, plus a red edge on the round tick key. Put Home's `leds` meter (open against late) in the page head's signal line. Hide the status tag when it equals the filter. Set the due line in var(--num) with tabular figures, and in words ("due Sun 27 Sep, 19:56") once views allows it.

Give the type a scale with real steps. The sheet uses nine sizes between 11.5 and 16px (11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 14.5, 15, 16) and nothing between the 34px `.page-head h1` and the 15px `.section-head h2`. So on Home, "coming up", "to do" and "lately added" are no bigger than the rows under them (`.card h2` is 16px, plan titles 15px). Define `--t-label 11.5px`, `--t-meta 13px`, `--t-body 15px`, `--t-head 19px`, `--t-title 34px` and map every rule to one of them. Set `.section-head h2` to 19px/1.2, weight 600, -0.012em. Raise `.chip-mon`/`.chip-dow` from 10.5 to 11.5px. Put `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every time, date chip and relative tag.

designs.name: Bench Scope
designs.tagline: The family's weeks traced across a bench oscilloscope: one size of engraved type on an instrument-grey panel, ivory legends, oxblood knobs, and phosphor only where the beam is.
designs.concept: Every page is the front panel of a bench oscilloscope. It is an instrument-grey plate screwed to a green-black rack, and engraved frames group its parts: each frame's name is set into its top line and its way on into its bottom line. A brushed aluminium nameplate names each page. The one picture is the scope, and it draws the family's own data: Home's coming four weeks as pulses, with now as the rose trigger; Ideas in XY mode; the Plans month on the glass. Every word is set at 15px, and hierarchy comes from weight, case, width, colour and space. The feel is calm and precise, like a well-labelled lab instrument at night, lit green only where the beam is.
designs.companions: OKLCH hue 7 has two materials with separate jobs. Oxblood (#7a3345, highlight #a0495e) is the hand: the knob caps that carry the family's initials, and the two bezel knobs, which now appear only on Home, sign-in and 404. Rose (#dd8899) is now and pointing, and never a state. It draws the trigger (a ▼ on the top edge of Home's graticule, a dashed line down the glass, a ▶ on the axis), '▼ now' set into the top line of today's cell in the month, the settings band-switch pointer, the fold triangles, the arrows on the ways on, and link underlines in prose only. Ivory (#e6ddca) fills the legends and headings, and khaki (#c0b39c) fills the labels, readouts and the 'changed' mark. Both are warm, low-chroma and material. The section colours (lilac, cyan, lemon, amber, pink, coral, sage outing) are scope channels. They show up as a bar lamp, the strip on a nameplate, a kind's name and icon, or a plan's cyan trace segment, and never as a fill behind words. Amber alone means 'needs a look': the setup frame, 'was due' on Home, the Needs-a-look tag, and the late lamp on To do when the view supplies it. Unlit lamps are dark lenses, not rose rings.
decisions: The dice's twist holds: one size, 15px on a 24px line, for every word. Hierarchy now has five named steps: 900 the question, 800 nameplate, 700 legend, 600 title/label, 400 body. Readouts are IBM Plex Mono with tabular, slashed-zero figures.

The engraver's cut (Archivo at 125% width) is kept for exactly three things: the nameplate, the frame legends and Home's question. Everything printed, including nav, keys, labels, frame-line links, tabs and facts, is at 100% width, weight 600 and 0.08em tracking. The width marks engraving, not size.

Home's question 'What's on your mind?' is the one sentence-case line in the engraver's cut: 900, 125%, 0.02em, with 'mind' in phosphor and 16px of air before the field. It is the page's h1 and serves as Home's nameplate, so Home has no aluminium plate.

Frames are the layout primitive on every page. The legend sits in the top line and the way on in the bottom line. Home's three columns now stretch so their bottom lines are one line. The Wishes page's kids became frames too, each with its three lists side by side.

The trace means what it draws. Each plan's day offset is worked out from its own date and today's words, using whole-number calendar arithmetic in _ui.html; it is no longer read back from radar distances. Pulse height is the number of plans that day, one step each. The next plan is intensified (brighter, thicker, filled), not taller. A dotted cursor with 'OCT' marks where the month turns. Plans more than 4 weeks off show as an arrow at the right edge.

Time belongs on the scope: the date left the speaker line and became a 'TUE 29 SEP' readout at the glass's top right, with the full date kept for screen readers. This removed the orphaned date line on the phone.
One live prompt per page. The bar's caret is lit and steady as part of the mark. The Next-up cursor is steady and dim. On Home only the question's cursor blinks.

Coming up rows say the date once: the readout chip gives the day (a fixed 12ch, so titles align), and the row gives '10:00 · in 2 days' in readout figures. The whole row is the target and lights with the afterglow, so titles in rows lose their underline. Plans-list rows, which carry their own keys, keep theirs.

Targets are real, not pseudo. The tick is a 44px button with its 30px key drawn by ::before. Frame-line links, kids' names, the short links in the glass and the setup link are 44px to the hand. Field mics are 44px with a smaller drawn knob. Home dropped from 24 targets under 44 to 5.

One plate width for every page: the chat keeps the 1232px plate and runs its conversation as a 944px column inside it. The box's own label 'Message to Vera' is now its frame legend, replacing the cold 'Input'.

To do speaks the instrument's language: the due date is a readout ('SUN 27 SEP 19:56', weekday computed in the template). The status tag is quiet (khaki outline, no lamp) and is shown only when the list mixes statuses.
One lit RUN key per page holds on the Family page too: the header's jump to the form is a grey key, and the form's Add is lit.

designs.name: Night Timetable
designs.tagline: A station at night: her conversation on the concourse, every other part of the house a numbered line in enamel colour, and the phosphor lit only on the departure boards and what is live.
designs.concept: FamilyDB is laid out as a well-signed railway station after dark, and Vera's conversation is its main line. On Home a track runs down the middle column: it starts at her screen, passes the box you write to her in (the stop you are at), runs through the ways to start, and ends at a terminus ring, "Continue with Vera". The Chat page is her line's printed timetable, with the time by each stop. Everything else is timetables under numbered enamel line signs (1 Vera, 2 Ideas, 3 Plans, 4 To do, 5 Wishes): slate plates, warm white type, khaki condensed labels and yellow wayfinding. The #6dff9c phosphor glows only on the departure boards and on whatever is live, so the page feels calm, legible and grounded.
designs.companions: Wayfinding yellow #ebd382 (the accent) has one job, showing the way: links, the arrow tiles, crumbs, the chevrons on selects and folds, 'you are here' (today's date tile and month cell, the current settings stop, the current facility tile), and posted notices (the calmed works stripe and the notice's step rings). It no longer goes on status icons, fold summaries or the phone's Home tile when that is not the current page. Each line has a lower-chroma enamel colour, used on its bullet, its nameboard band, the band under the bar, its table's top rule, its tab underline and now the rule under its sign on Home: heather #b694d5 for Ideas, sky slate #99d4f3 for Plans, teal #89d4cf for To do, rose #e6a0ba for Wishes, and the calm lit green #8ce1a4 for Vera's line, rail, stops and terminus. Copper #ebab72 is for people: family initials, the warm #272017 tint of their bubbles, restaurants, 'was due' and 'needs a look'. Red #f2716a is kept for what went wrong. Neutrals: green-black ground #0b100d, slate plates #0f1a1c, warm ink #e9e6dd, khaki labels #b7b19c.
decisions: A clean sheet, now about 105 KB (variants/r10-wild-3/sheet.css), with my own base.html, _ui.html, home.html, ideas.html, and now chat.html and tasks.html. No form, field, link or icon was removed, and removed.txt is empty.

The numbered-lines grammar is kept everywhere. Numbers sit in discs only for lines. The facilities (Home, Memory, Family, Status, Settings) are square slate pictogram tiles, and a tile turns yellow only when it is the current page.

Home is the concourse. A posted notice runs as a strip across the top of all three columns while setup is unfinished, with its steps drawn as a horizontal line diagram. Below it are three columns: the departures on the left, Vera's line in the middle, To do and Lately added on the right. The middle column stays in view as you scroll where the screen is tall enough (sticky at 70rem wide and 46rem tall and up). In the source and on a phone she comes first and the notice follows her.

Vera's line on Home: her screen, then her '1' bullet, her name and the date. A 6px rail runs down the left of the column. The box has its own stop ring with a connector, and the ring lights in the phosphor while you write. The ways to start are a vertical list of ticket stops. 'Continue with Vera' is always drawn as the terminus ring. On a phone the box takes the full width and the rail runs behind it.

Chat is a printed timetable in a 52rem column with three columns: time, track, stop. The time is set right against the rail in condensed tabular figures, with the day under it only where the day changes. A repeated day stays in the page as visually hidden text, so a screen reader still hears it. Every bubble starts from one left edge, and her text runs to 62ch. The newest stop and its time are lit in the phosphor. The box is the next stop in the stop column, with the rail running on into its ring. The nameboard is compact, so the box starts about 75px higher. On a phone the time sits at the top right of each bubble.

Board type rule: the dot-matrix face Doto is used only for a board's tag (.inverse) and titles of 1.5rem and up: Next up's title, the radar's count, the spend figure and the 404. Every smaller board line is DM Mono 500 at 1rem, in the same phosphor, with its glow halved. The dim phosphor mix goes from 74% to 84%.

Type system: nine named steps (--t-name to --t-label). Archivo in three widths: 112% for the nameboards, her question and now the month title; normal for reading; 75 to 85% condensed with tabular figures for labels, stamps, times and dates. The links in section signs are now condensed capital labels in khaki with the yellow arrow tile, so counts no longer read like line numbers.
Line numbers now do something: each line in the bar has accesskey 1 to 5, with aria-keyshortcuts and a title such as 'Line 1 · Alt+1'.

Plans month is printed like a timetable sheet: hairlines on the ground, weekends a 3% tint, and days outside the month shown as faint numerals on the same ground. Only a day with a plan takes the slate plate and a 3px sky rule. Today keeps its yellow tile and outline. The Plans list panel gets the line's top rule like every other list.

Status lamps: 'on' is the phosphor dot with a glow, 'off' is an unlit ring (edge colour on the field colour), 'part' is half copper, and red appears only inside a trouble panel. The lit lamps are now the only light on the page.

Controls: selects use appearance: base-select with a yellow chevron, a yellow top rule on the list and a lit-green dot on the chosen option. The Kind field (a list input) now wears the same yellow chevron, with the browser's grey arrow hidden underneath but still clickable. Placeholders are weight 400. Checkboxes are ticked in the lit green. One brand focus ring everywhere. Every fold's words are ink-2 and only its chevron is yellow.

(2) Always draw her rail: drop the :has(.thread.brief) guard on .welcome-words::before and run it from her screen, down the left of .ask, through the starters. (3) Make .welcome .starters a vertical stop list on that rail: flex-direction: column, each ticket with a small ring stop. (4) Always end the list with .brief-more 'Continue with Vera →' as the terminus ring, whether or not there is a line. Optionally make .welcome sticky (position: sticky; top: 5.5rem) at 70rem and up, with the column hairlines moved to .departures' border-right and .around's border-left, so she stays in view while the timetables scroll.

That leaves a ragged left edge (her two bubbles start at x=153 and x=207), so the eye zigzags. The sheet's own promise, 'the time printed by the stop, as a timetable does', is not drawn: the time sits inside the bubble. Fix: make it a printed timetable. From 44rem up use grid-template-columns: 5.5rem 3rem minmax(0, 1fr) (time, track, stop) inside the centred 46rem column. Put every bubble in column 3 with max-width: none and .said-text at max-width: 62ch. firstDraft.name: Night Timetable
firstDraft.concept: The app is laid out as a railway at night. Vera's conversation is the concourse in the middle of Home, and on the Chat page it is a track down the centre with every message a stop. Everything else sits around it as a printed timetable under numbered line signs: 1 Vera, 2 Ideas, 3 Plans, 4 To do, 5 Wishes. It should feel calm, legible and grounded, like a well-signed station after dark: slate-enamel plates, warm white type, khaki timetable labels and yellow wayfinding. The #6dff9c phosphor glows only on the dot-matrix departure boards and on whatever is live.

designs.name: Figure Ground
designs.tagline: The family's operator manual: every part a numbered plate led by its own figure, drawn in blueprint blue on green-black, with the phosphor lit only where the machine is live.
designs.concept: Brutalism read as an operator's manual. Every page is a numbered chapter that matches its cell in the ruled bar. Every part of a page is a numbered plate: a ruled row with a figure drawn from the page's own data on the left, the words on the right, and a hairline running down the page between them. The feel is a calm, well-set technical manual lit by one green tube: square, ruled and plain, with underlined blue links. #6dff9c appears only where the machine is live, and now the figure also lights whatever you point at or type in.
designs.companions: Blueprint blue (OKLCH hue 261) has two jobs. Every link is #94bbfe and underlined, including the month's event links now. Every drawing is in #617ba7 lines with #88a5d7 labels on a 12px grid, and the month's event edges and the Ideas bars now use that ink too. Paper grey #d4d4c9 means only 'you are here' in reverse video: the current bar cell, tab, settings part, the chosen company card and the chosen select row. A darker paper, #8d8f86, draws the 3px page rules. Amber means only 'late or needs a look': late cells in the tally, late nodes in the queue, the LATE tag with an amber due line, setup rungs, the warning tag. Kind colours appear only as legend squares, on rows, bars, the collection and the anatomy's kind box. Kind words are label grey. Green is kept to the mark and caret, primary buttons, 'mind', focus, lamps, ticks, today (the ring in the month, the key and the chip), the NOW line in the queue, the newest arrow, the lit machine part and the lit form part, the afterglow edge, and the monitors.
decisions: Clean sheet (93 KB) with 17 of my own templates: base, _ui, _ask, _machine, a new _anatomy, home, chat, ideas, idea (new), plans (new), plans_month, tasks, status, settings, settings_section, idea_form, login and 404. No static files. Every drawing is inline SVG, aria-hidden, and says in words beside it what it shows. removed.txt is empty: no field, form, action, link or icon is lost.

One figure system: the fig() macro wraps each drawing in a <details> that is always open on a wide screen (::details-content forced visible). On a phone the drawing becomes a 5.5rem thumbnail floated beside the plate's heading, with its FIG number and a +/- box; a tap opens the whole drawing and a second tap closes it. The summary is out of the Tab order because the drawing only repeats the plate's words. Monitors keep their size.

One numbering scheme: chapter.plate for plates (the h2 numbers, now also on section panels, settings panels and folds), FIG. N.N for figures, CHAPTER N over titles, circled numerals for the machine's parts everywhere (the diagram, the Settings key, the settings nav and the bar's menu, which no longer says 10.1-10.9). All generated numbers carry empty alt text (content: ... / ""). The Settings list is headed KEY TO FIG. 10.1, and General's panels are 10.2 onward.

Figures follow their own ink rule and share their legends. One tally() macro draws Home FIG 1.3 and To do FIG 5.1 with the same legend (LATE amber, DUE shaded, NO DATE outline, DONE lit when present), both using Household. The To do queue is keyed by #id and date only, with a green dashed NOW line drawn between past and future deadlines and late nodes in amber. The Ideas kinds chart uses drawing-ink bars with a kind square at each label. Drawing text is 12 units, and --fig-w never drops below 16rem.

No data, no figure: with nothing open or waiting, Home's wishes plate is one ruled line ('1.5 The kids' wishes  Maya 0 open · Theo 0 open  ALL'). It keeps the empty figure column so the hairline runs on.

The figure lights what you are on, in CSS alone with no script. Hovering or focusing a part in the Settings key or the settings nav rings its callout on the machine. Focusing a field on the new or edit idea form lights that part of the anatomy. Both light instantly and fade over the 900ms afterglow.

Plans month FIG 4.1 is now a Key to the month, drawn with the grid's own marks: today (ring and lit date block, showing the real day), a plan, from Google (dashed edge), weekend band and another month (hatched). The plans list gets FIG 4.2, the next five weeks as a small month (today ringed, a bar under each planned day), computed in Jinja from ISO dates.

The idea page is templated as three plates. FIG 3.1 draws this idea's record the way the form's anatomy draws a new one: known parts solid, unknown dashed, and its kind square in the kind box. Then 3.2 What to do with it (calendar, Plan it, Record how it went, outcomes) and 3.3 The place, where an opening-hours bar chart replaces the picto when hours are known. Edit and Drop sit in an actions row.

Typesetting: every sentence is in Plex Sans 14px/1.45 or larger (source note, time-zone note, hints, 'No active reminder.', did, the save bar, #where, the NOTE flash). Mono is kept for labels, numbers and dates. Figure captions are Plex Sans italic, the system's only italic. Tabular figures on .when, the chip day, counts and plate numbers. The task title is 18px. Disclosures are ink-2 mono caps with the [+] box and are never blue.

Targets: inline links carry padding-block max(0.1em, (25px - 1.28em)/2), so every link in running text is a 24px target without moving the line. Checkboxes are 24px. Each Ideas row is one target through a stretched title link. Rings on bar, menu and nav cells are inset (-4px). The lone arrow on each Settings row is gone.

The bar narrows by turning the household's words into icons first and keeps the chapter numbers down to 60rem. There is no sideways scroll at 840, 900, 1000 or 1100px. On a phone the tab bar puts each chapter number above its word.

The phone's first screen: the hub gives way to a ruled three-cell strip (5 PLANS | 12 IDEAS | 4 TO DO); the question is 2.125rem; the ask bar is two rows (From and mic, then Send where I am and Send), so the starters show above the tab bar. On Chat the sequence diagram folds to one ruled line (FIG. 2.2 [+]), so the first message sits near 330px instead of 555px.

Other pages brought into the system with CSS: the Family list as ruled rows with initial squares; the AI model page's company cards as ruled cells, the chosen one in paper; the wish lists in three columns with circled ranks; memory rows; the setup steps as ruled rows with circled numbers (amber until done, lit once done); setup progress as tabs. Sticky offsets come from a --bar-h token.

Make one rule for under 52rem: a data figure becomes a 5.5rem thumbnail beside its plate heading. Generalise the existing `.page-head:has(> .fig-picto)` grid to `.plate:has(> .fig)`. The full drawing stays behind the FIG. line as a <details> that opens on a tap. Monitors keep their size. Replace the hub on the phone with a ruled three-cell strip (5 PLANS | 12 IDEAS | 4 TO DO), at most 2.75rem tall. Set `.welcome h1` and `.ask-question label` to 2.125rem. The tab bar (.places at ≤52rem) loses the chapter numbers the whole idea rests on: put the `.ch` '03' above each word (the tabs are already column-flex at 3.6rem).

ONE NUMBERING SCHEME. Today three collide. The bar menu numbers the parts '10.1 General … 10.6' (base.html line 90, `10.{{ loop.index }}`), which clashes with FIG. 10.1. The machine diagram and the settings nav use circled 1–9. General's 'Where home is' and the Settings index list carry no plate number at all. Use chapter.plate for plates and circled ①–⑨ for parts everywhere, including the menu (reuse `.part-no`). Put the numbers on the General and Settings index plates. At 72–78rem, hide the tools' words (`.tools .label`) before `.bar .ch`, and keep the numbers down to 52rem. Give the generated numbers empty alt text, `content: var(--ch) '.' counter(plate) / ''` and `'CHAPTER ' var(--ch) / ''`, so a screen reader says 'Coming up', not 'one point two Coming up'.

FIGURES MUST OBEY THEIR OWN INK RULE, AND THEIR LEGENDS MUST AGREE. (a) Ideas FIG 3.2 fills its bars in full kind colours (.kind-fill .k-*) and is the loudest colour on the page. Draw the bars as `.d-cell.dated` (draw-fill with a draw-2 stroke) and put a 10-unit kind square at each label, as rule 2 says. (b) Home's tally uses LATE/DUE/NO DATE with amber for late and a column called '—'. To do's FIG 5.1 uses DEADLINE/NONE/DONE, has no amber, and calls the column 'Household', even though two tasks are late. Make one `tally()` macro with one legend, and use Household in both. (c) FIG 5.2 cuts titles short ('#4 CALL THE DENTIST…'): key it by #id and date only, since the rows below give the words. (d) `.d-key` at 9.5 and `.d-label` at 10 units in a 256 viewBox render at about 7.7px when --fig-w is 13rem. Raise them to 12 units and keep --fig-w at 16rem or more. (e) Plans FIG 4.1, the 35-day strip, is unreadable: 7-unit days, unlabelled blocks and no caption. Make it 'Key to the month' instead, drawn with the calendar's own marks: today ring, plan bar, dashed = from Google, weekend band, hatched = outside. The grid itself is the drawing, and nothing explains those marks yet.

COLOUR JOBS LEAK. `.kind { color: var(--kc) }` colours the kind word: ACTIVITY in yellow, RESTAURANT in amber and OUTING in green sit beside blue titles, so Home's Lately rows and every Ideas row read as a rainbow. Set `.kind` to var(--label) and leave colour on `.swatch` only, as the pitch promised. `.restaurants-link .eyebrow` ('SOMETHING TO EAT') is amber: make it --label. `.status-open` puts a gold OPEN tag on every To do row while the overdue rows go unmarked ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56'). Drop OPEN under the Open filter and give overdue rows `.tag.warn` LATE with an amber due line, so amber has one meaning. `.chip-mon` 'OCT' is in --plans cyan right next to #94bbfe links: move it to --label so there is one blue family. The 3px rules (bar, under the head, colophon) are in --ink-2 at about 11:1 and glare. Draw them in a darker paper (about #8d8f86) and keep #d4d4c9 for reverse video only.

NO DATA, NO FIGURE; LET THE FIGURE AND THE WORDS WORK TOGETHER. With nothing open, Home's FIG 1.5 is six dashed slots, which is decoration. That plate should become `.plate.span`, one ruled line: '1.5 The kids' wishes · Maya 0 open · Theo 0 open  ALL →'. That also shortens Home, which runs to about 2630px on desktop with To do, Setup, Wishes and Lately below the first screen. Consider moving 'Finish setting up' (amber, needs a look) to 1.2, as today's page does. FIG 1.6 could colour all 12 squares by kind (a waffle chart of the collection) and outline the 4 newest in ink. Carry the 'lit part' idea further in CSS alone: `main:has(.section-card:nth-child(3):hover) .d-call-3` lights a callout on the Settings index, and `main:has(#f-title:focus) .d-field-title { stroke: var(--brand) }` lights the form anatomy's field as you type in it. Then the figure lights what you are on, on every page.

TYPESETTING. Whole sentences are set in 13px mono: `.source` ('Google Calendar is not connected…'), `.zone`, `.fig figcaption` ('North at the top…'), 'No active reminder.' and `.did`. Move them to Plex Sans at 0.875rem/1.45 and keep mono for labels, numbers and dates. Set figure captions in Plex Sans Italic, as a manual would; italic appears nowhere else in the system, so it gives captions their own voice. Add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to `.when`, `.chip-day` and `.d-count`. Bring `.task-head h2` (19px, off the scale) to 18px. Give disclosures one style: `.task details.more > summary` ('EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE') is blue, so it looks like a link. Make it ink-2 mono caps with the [+] box, like 'Add something to do', and keep blue for navigation only.

TARGETS AND FOCUS. There are 13 inline links under 24px on Ideas and 9 on To do. Make each ruled row a single target: `position: relative` on `.idea-table > .idea-card` and a stretched `::after { inset: 0 }` on its title link, with `--surface-2` on hover. Give the Nearest/Furthest caption links `padding-block: 0.2em`. Bar cells: at `outline-offset: 2px` the top of the ring is cut off by the viewport (focus-4). Use `.places a:focus-visible, .tools a:focus-visible { outline-offset: -4px }`. The Settings index puts a lone → at the far right of each row, about 750px from the title, which leaves a dead sight line. Drop it, or make the whole row the link.

FINISH THE PAGES THAT WERE NOT TEMPLATED, SO THE SYSTEM READS AS THE APP'S STANDARD. The idea detail page stacks Edit and Drop and has no figure plate: give it FIG 3.1 (its own blip on the radar rings, with its distance and kind square) and an `.actions` row. Plans month event links (`.event a`) are in ink with a grey underline, which breaks 'every link is blue': use var(--link). The plans list, Wishes, Family and Memory should get the same page-head figure or picto and numbered plates. The form anatomy's '+ INDOOR, WEATHER, COST, TIMES, SEASONS' runs past its inner box: wrap it onto two lines. firstDraft.name: Figure Ground
firstDraft.concept: This is brutalism taken as an operator's manual. The structure is on show: every page is a numbered chapter, the same number as its cell in the bar. Every part of a page is a numbered plate: a ruled row with a FIGURE on the left and the words on the right, and a hairline running down the page between them. The figures come first and are drawn from the page's own data: a hub of what Vera keeps, a radar, a tally of whose tasks are whose, a sequence diagram of the conversation, a wiring diagram of what is connected, and a parts diagram of the machine that is also the key to Settings. The feel is a calm, well-set technical manual lit by one green tube: square, ruled and plain, with underlined blue links, and #6dff9c only where the machine is live.

designs.name: Figured Atlas
designs.tagline: A star atlas with its figures drawn in: every row of the app hangs from a round chart in the margin (an idea's constellation, a plan's date, a task's unlit star), names set in Fraunces, speech in Plex Sans, the catalogue in Plex Mono, and the phosphor kept for the console.
designs.concept: Porcelain Atlas's star atlas, bound as a book: one centred column on a green-black dome with a cobalt zenith. Each kind of idea is drawn in as a constellation on its own double-ruled round chart. This revision makes the chart the rule for the whole app. Every catalogue row (ideas, plans, tasks, settings, the kids) hangs from a round mark in the left margin with a dotted leader, and the names keep the column's edge under the page title. It should feel calm, typeset and a little storybook, with #6dff9c lit only where the machine is.

decisions: The chart is the system, not only the kinds. The double-ruled round chart (.figure) is now shared by four marks. An idea's figure is the constellation. A plan's date is the month in caps over the day in Plex Mono 400, in teal, amber for today. A settings part is its line icon in a porcelain ring, amber when it needs a look. A kid is her initial in a rose ring. People in the chat are rings too; Vera alone keeps her square screen, so people are round and the machine is square.

One hanging rule at 64rem and wider. Every catalogue's mark is set absolutely at right: calc(100% + var(--hang)), with --hang 1.6rem, so all marks stand right-aligned on one vertical. Each has a dotted leader in its own colour to the words, and the words keep the column's edge. The rule covers Ideas, Restaurants, Coming up on Home, the Plans list, the idea page's On the calendar, Home's To do, the To do page, Settings and the kids' wishes on Home. Below 64rem the same marks sit inline in a first column.

A task is a star not yet lit. The tick and the task box are a small ring (1.3rem, edge hairline, field fill). Pointed at, the ring glows lemon and shows a four-point star (a new i-lit symbol in the sprite, used by the tick macro). Pressed or done, it becomes the lit sage four-point star (the --spark clip-path, from the figures' sparkle). Setup steps on Home are amber rings for the same reason.

Ideas pacing. The radar now comes after the list. Search, Status, For and Filter are on one row, and the key of figures is a band under them, so DOM order and Tab order follow the eye. The page head is a grid: title and action on one row, the lede at full measure below it, so the lede is one line on desktop. 'Save a thought for later' is a slim row when folded, and main's top padding is 3.75rem. Two figured rows are now in the first 900px (the second in part); on the phone the first idea arrives at about 1.1 screens instead of 1.7.

The key keeps 5 columns × 2 rows: figures at 2.1rem, stroke-opacity .8, names tracked .04em, so RESTAURANT clears Seasonal. Below 30rem it is one row that scrolls sideways inside itself, each figure over its name in 5.4rem snap columns, with a fade at the right edge and no scroll bar. On the phone the filter boxes are Search; Status; For with Filter beside it.

Home: Lately added (the plate of four charts) moved in markup to straight after the welcome, so it sits under Next up and the Tab order stays honest. The rhythm is one 3rem step: welcome margin 3rem and padding 2.25rem, every section 3rem apart. The page is now 2820px, down from 2970.

Idea page. One column, as the book is. The 6.5rem figure is a centred frontispiece over centred kind caps, a Fraunces title up to 3.052rem and the meta line, closed by a full-measure rule; the facts and description follow at the measure. Place facts sit in one column, and an empty place fact list is hidden. The side column's heads use the plans teal. Today on the idea's calendar is worked out from plan.relative == 'today', because plan_row has no on_today.

Links and labels are told apart. Section links, crumbs, 'Continue with' and '.links' are in their part's accent, with a 1px underline at 35% and the arrow or plus icon back (inline-flex, 0.9em). Things pressed (buttons, nav, tabs, settings nav) moved up to a second catalogue step, --t-key 0.8125rem; labels stay at --t-cat 0.75rem. Focus is a 2px green outline at a 3px offset.

Figure line strength is set by size. stroke-opacity was taken out of every line group in the sprite (the sky's dashed arc keeps .4). CSS now sets it: .62 on charts, .8/1.35 in the key, .85/1.45 in the form legend, and 1/1.7 on the tab and kind icons, so the small sky and bowl read.

Plans month on the phone (a variant plans_month.html). Each busy day has the same date chart, the day name in catalogue caps (amber today) and the square TODAY pill, then its events one to a line. On the desktop grid, today is an amber double-ruled ring instead of a filled square.

New-idea form: the figures are a legend inside the Kind field. Figures are 1.75rem, 3×3, named in Plex Sans 14px dim lowercase (the speaking voice), with nothing to press. They read as a key to type from, and the datalist still offers the words.

Kept from the first draft: the three faces with one job each on the 1.25 scale, 'mind' in the Fraunces WONK italic in phosphor, square plates, one hairline weight, the cobalt dome and margin stars, the transcript chat and every token and glow number.

Remove the attribute from the line groups (stroke-opacity is inherited through `<use>`) and set it by size in CSS: `.figure .icon { stroke-opacity: .62 }`, `.figures-key .figure .icon { stroke-opacity: .8; stroke-width: 1.35 }`, `.tabs .icon, .kind .icon { stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-width: 1.7 }`. Leave the sky's dashed path at .4.

Two corners outside the system. (a) The Plans month on the phone (`.month-list`) still sets the day in Plex Sans 600 amber with each `.event` inline-block squeezed to its right. Set `.month-list li > strong` in the catalogue voice (Plex Mono, `--t-cat`, caps, `--label`, `--people` for `.today`), `.month-list .event { display: block; margin: .45rem 0 0 }`, and the day as the same chip as Coming up. firstDraft.name: Figured Atlas
firstDraft.concept: This keeps Porcelain Atlas, a star atlas bound as a book with one centred column on a green-black dome, and draws the atlas's figures into it. Each kind of idea is now a constellation: a faint line picture of the thing (a bowl, a kite, a mountain, a ship, a car, a lyre, a leaf, a garland, a comet), with its stars in the kind's colour and one bright four-pointed star. designs.name: Evening Listing
designs.tagline: The programme guide finished: heads that hold one line, links that read as links, a steel block for where you are, facts in true columns, one pewter line to each band, and #6dff9c lit only where the machine is live.
designs.concept: Programme Guide, finished rather than redrawn. It keeps the TV-listing structure that won every lens: slate bands with the head column inside, one-line rows read along a dotted leader to the facts, condensed Instrument Sans heads, Plex Mono figures, the tuning scale and the thin grooved case. What changes is the finish the judges asked for: every head holds one line, links look like links, "here" is a steel reverse block that survives the squint, the facts sit in fixed tabular columns, and each band gets one quiet pewter line. The feel is an evening TV listing lit by one green tube, calm and easy to scan, where the bright phosphor means live.
designs.companions: Every companion is a solid colour with one job, and none of them glows. Denim #9db6d6 is for every link made of words: underlined, sentence case, with an arrow ("All plans →", "Change a key →", the crumbs). Steel #748a9b with #0b0e0c ink (about 5.5:1) is reverse video for "you are here": the bar's current place and tool, the Settings menu and nav, the view tabs, and today on the month. On the phone, the current tab is a tinted solid #26313a with a 2px #a7c2d5 cap and its label in the heading colour. Pewter #47535b is the one line to each band, and the ring round the icon of a one-list page. Slate (band #10161a, zebra #161d22, cards #151b1e, edge #2e343b, bar #0f1417) grounds every list on every page. The cobalt wash #4f60e6 at 2.4 is the greeting's second light, sampled at (23,36,46). The accent #84a0c4 stays on the icons of pages with no colour of their own, to hold the protan floor. Outing moves to a celadon #9fcfb6 (C 0.061), so the kind no longer reads as the brand. Amber keeps its one job: needs a look, and late. The full #6dff9c stays on the mark, Send, "mind", focus, the live status lamps, the monitors, and the new breathing now lamp. Sage #86d9a6 lights the ticks, the typed-in box and the short lit segment on the tuning scale.
decisions: Heads never wrap. The head column is 11.75rem at 72rem and wider. Heads are 1.3rem condensed (wdth 80, 600) with nowrap and balance, and the icon hangs in a 1.75rem indent, so every note and link in the head column lines up under the head's words. Measured at 1280: 'Finish setting up' is 153px in a 160px measure, and every h2 is one 21px line. Curly apostrophes are used in 'The kids’ wishes' and 'The kids’ conversations'. Chat's kids band takes a 15rem head column, because its rows are only names.

Below 72rem the head sits above its rows, with the icon, head, link and note on one line (checked at 1100px). On the phone, band padding is trimmed. Coming up's day words become screen-reader-only there, because the date leaf shows the date, and its time and relative day move under the title. Lately's 'for …' also moves under the title, and the Next up tube is compacted. The phone Home is 2491px against Programme Guide's 2865px.

Links: Instrument Sans 500 at .9rem, sentence case, denim #9db6d6, a 1px underline at .2em offset, an arrow icon and a 44px hit box. Mono caps (.74rem, weight 500, .04em) are kept only for labels, counts, captions and eyebrows. Links on the tubes stay phosphor (a :not(.crt *) guard).

'Here' is the steel reverse block everywhere: bar places, tools, the Settings menu summary and list, the settings nav, the tabs, and today on the month (the day number in steel). The tuning scale lights a 2px sage segment under the block, and under the brand on Home. The squint strip shows the block clearly on Ideas and Chat.

Bent brief (3): the view switches (All ideas | Restaurants, List | Month) are a horizontal pair, but they sit on the page's own line directly under the title, not between the filters and the rows. There they stay in one place when you switch views, because Restaurants has no filter. They are also right above everything they switch, and they are held by the ring-and-line the owner called one of the best elements yet. The count ('12 ideas') sits at the right end of that line.

Line art, one line per band. A 1px pewter line drops from the head's icon down the head column, turns one 8px rounded corner under the last row, runs under the rows and ends in a 6px tick at the facts end. It is drawn on bands, pair parts and Status's lower panels, and hidden below 72rem. On one-list pages (Ideas, Restaurants, Plans, To do) the page icon is ringed. The line drops from the ring and turns under the tabs, or under the To do finder. This is drawn with the page head's own grid (a ::before grid item), so it cannot drift. There are no rings on band icons and no buffer stops.

Facts are truly tabular, with fixed sub-columns in the facts' own ch units. Coming up: the day words right-aligned, then time 5ch and relative 10ch in Plex Mono, with the day numerals right-aligned in the designator. Ideas: drive 11ch right-aligned ('2 h 05 min' padded) | way 2ch | for 9.5rem | # 3.5ch. The drive is shortened in the template, and the full 'about 27 min south of home (estimate)' is kept for screen readers. Home To do: owner column | due 20ch. A leader is drawn only when a detail or facts cell follows (:has). Rows are capped at 62rem.
The kind moves beside the title, in its own colour (500 .8rem). This clears the facts column and keeps the 'kind named in its colour' trait on both Home and Ideas.
Field labels are Plex Mono 500 at .74rem, uppercase, .04em, including the month's weekday heads and the date leaves. VT323 remains only on the tubes, the greeting date and FROM.
The now lamp is a breathing #6dff9c lamp (2.4s) in the designator of Coming up's next plan, and it is still under prefers-reduced-motion.

Brief (8), met another way: on Status, Who answers and Keys set their lamp rows two abreast (an annunciator board) at 72rem and wider, with zebra in pairs. This keeps each band's head column and line. What it has cost starts at 748px, and its $0.00 figure is above the fold at 1280×900.

To do rebuilt. The page's line holds Show, then Search, then Filter on one row. Under it: '4 shown (up to 100)' and the time-zone note, then the add fold, then one-line rows. Each row has a square tick well, #id and title, a slate OPEN tag, a leader and the owner. The facts cell holds 'Due 27 Sep 19:56' in tabular mono, with a figure space so single-digit days align, over 'No active reminder.' The edit fold is at the row's end. The template has no 'today', so 'was due 2 days ago' cannot be shown here.

Amber keeps one job. OPEN tags are slate. Setup steps are drawn identically at rest: a hover no longer fills the row, it only firms the amber underline. The lit third step came from the pointer left over from the sign-in click.

Chat: each speaker's name and time sit in their own outer gutter. Vera's are right-aligned left of her screen, and the family's are left-aligned right of their initial. The family bubble's steel cap moves to its right edge, and the chat column widens to 62rem. On the phone, the name and time share the avatar's row and bubbles run the full width from the gutter edge, about 36 characters a line.
The greeting's Next up column is 21.5rem, so Send stays on the From row with the wider head column. On a tube, the '4 more on the radar' link keeps a 44px target.
The css is written as a readable source (variants/r10-idea-1/palette.css, built by build.py, 30.5k of the 60k budget), so the standard can be read and ported.

designs.name: Docked Terminal
designs.tagline: The machine gets one lit glass column of its own, docked beside a grounded slate desk mat where the family's things are worked with real indigo keys.
designs.concept: The owner asked for bright green where the motif needs it and grounded colour elsewhere, and this design makes that the page's layout. On every page where the machine has something to show, it gets one rounded column of green-black glass at the left (Vera's screen and question, the ask box, Next up, the radar, the spend tube, the sign-in face, the 404 scope), lit by a green pool rising from its foot and a cobalt wash in its top corner. The family's things lie beside it on one square slate mat and are worked with real keys: raised indigo keys to press, sunk wells to type in, and a latched, lit indigo key for "here". It should feel like a calm terminal docked on a desk at night. The green lives in the glass, and the desk is slate, bone ink and the family's indigo hand.
designs.companions: Indigo (h262) is the second colour and has one job, the family's hand, carried only in solids. It fills every key that isn't the one green primary (face #192a4b, lit from above and falling to #111d35, skirt #0b172f, legend #d5dfef), the latched "here" (face #293f67 with a 2px #a4beef cap) in the bar, the tabs, the settings nav, the phone tab pill, today on the month and the checked option in pickers, and the family's chat bubbles (#132038 with a 2px #a4beef edge) and square avatars. A faint indigo tint also marks weekend columns on the month. There is no indigo glow anywhere. Links are an indigo chalk (#b8c8e5) with a mid-indigo underline (#738fc3), which is also the accent (title tiles on Home, Vera, Status and Settings, and the Home tab). Cobalt #4f60e6 appears only as the wash in the glass column's top corner. The desk is green-black slate (#10161a mat, #232b30 edge) with bone ink #d4cfc4, heading #ebe6da and cool label #a4b0c2. Sage #86d9a6 is for ticks, "on" lamps and outings. Amber keeps one job, "needs a look" (the setup plate's #644e29 edge, late dues). Red is only an "off" ring. Section and kind colours are unchanged: tinted 14% in the inlays for the cool kinds, 6% with only the icon coloured for the warm ones.
decisions: Layout is the idea. base.html gets a `machine` block, first in the DOM, and a `.desk` wrapper. From 64rem, `main:has(> .machine)` becomes a grid: a 23-25rem glass column (26rem from 88rem) beside a desk capped at 62rem, centred. The column is sticky at the bar's height plus 1.5rem when the viewport is 56rem or taller, with max-height set to the screen and overflow auto. Pages without a column (To do, Settings, Family, Memory, Wishes, forms) get a centred 62rem mat and never an empty rail. Below 64rem the column becomes a top block.

What each column holds. Home: Vera's screen with her name and date in VT323 phosphor, the question in condensed Archivo with the glowing 'mind', the textarea as a sunk well, From, select, mic and Send on one row, Send where I am, the ways to start as keys, then Next up in its case on a horizon with green airglow. Chat: her large screen, h1 and lede, a READY/WORKING state word (aria-hidden), then the composer. Ideas: the radar in portrait above its words. Plans: Next up. Status: the spend tube and a VT323 line of lamps for who answers. Sign in and 404: the tube, with the form or words on a short matching mat.

One row drawing on every list: an inlay designator (a date chip, kind, tick well, gift or setting icon), the title over its detail, and a facts column in Red Hat Mono with a slashed zero. Rows are at least 3.25rem with hairlines between them. Hover fills surface-2 with a 2px indigo edge that fades over 900ms. I moved facts (the relative day, the due, #N, 'N open') into their own cell in the templates so they align down the column.

Controls. Raised means press: 3px square keys, 2.75rem tall, with a 2px skirt and a 1px highlight, dropping 2px when pressed. The one #6dff9c key per page is Send, Add an idea or Save; every other key is indigo. Latched and lit means here: the chosen key is the lit one, never the sunk one, which answers Attract Mode's backwards latch. Sunk means type: every field is a well with a 3:1 edge and an inner shadow. Focus is a 2px #6dff9c ring at 2px offset with a 12px bloom, on checkboxes and on `select:open` too. Selects use `appearance: base-select` with a slate picker and a latched checked option. Checkboxes are 2.75rem targets that draw a 1.25rem sunk square, ticked in sage.
Lamps are round and flat: #6dff9c only for live (the models that answer now, the column's lamp line and state lamp), sage for on, amber for needs a look, a hollow red ring for off.

Monitors: a square #34393e case with .45rem sides, a 1px groove drawn in inset shadows, and a 0.95rem chin holding vents and a #6dff9c LED in one pseudo-element. A roll bar sweeps each tube once in 1.2s, starting at .35 opacity; it is hidden under reduced motion, and power-on content starts at .35, never 0. Next up stands on a horizon rule with a faint green airglow rising behind the chin.

Type: one pairing, each face with a job. Archivo condensed (stretch 78%, 650) for titles and heads, normal width to read, and expanded caps (118%, 600, .75rem, .04em) for labels, eyebrows, kind names and the small head and tab keys. Red Hat Mono tabular with a slashed zero for facts, times, ids and counts. VT323 only on the glass. The scale steps by 1.25: 2.44 / 1.95 / 1.56 / 1.25 / 1 / .8, with a .75 caps floor. Ledes and her lines are capped at 60ch, with text-wrap balance on heads and pretty on paragraphs.

Bent from the brief: the big action keys (Send, Save, the ways to start) keep sentence-case legends, and only the small head, tab and month keys use expanded caps. Lessons say all-caps buttons went unrewarded, and three starters in caps would not fit the column.

Both look as the brief asks, but they sit just under the metric's value threshold, so the indigo solids stop swamping the green-share figure (Chat 21% before, 53% now; Home 23%, now 29%). Tab order: the column comes first in the DOM, and _ask.html puts Send where I am after Send, so all 40 stops I recorded on Home follow the eye: bar, then glass, then the desk top to bottom.
